title: John and June Allcott Gallery: Michelle Inez Hinojosa and Barbara Pearsall
location: Hanes Art Center, John and June Allcott Gallery
description:
Art and Art History

Under the Tent: Whirling & Flickering

August 20-October 15, 2026

Reception: August 20, 5-7 pm

 

Drawn together in graduate school by their mutual love of experimentation and play, Michelle Inez Hinojosa and Barbara Pearsall have built a collaborative practice around analogue animation and vibrant abstraction. Together, their work explores optical toys, immersive installations, and movement. Under the Tent: Whirling & Flickering features kaleidoscopic imagery, flickering abstractions, projection mapping, a hidden trapdoor, and hand-cranked wheels that transform what viewers see. After searching for the perfect venue, they are thrilled to bring their collaborative installation to UNC. Their first public artwork, Turnabout Folly, will debut in Lansing, Michigan in Fall 2026.

 

Michelle Hinojosa works at the intersection of painting, poetry, and fiber art, where she considers memory, intergenerational trauma, and migration. Born in central Texas, by way of the fields of California and Northern Mexico, Michelle uplifts traditions of making that have provided much-needed stability to a family displaced. Michelle Hinojosa is an Assistant Professor of Art at Pennsylvania State University.

 

Barbara Pearsall is an artist and educator based in Michigan. Her art practice is attentive to how deviation from material conventions can subvert or metamorphose the role of institutions, where her philosophical and political concerns manifest through material explorations of the built environment. Her pieces seek to create illusory and unusual architectural conditions as a form of resistance, interrupting real-world functionality to allow for alternative systems of order. She is an Assistant Professor of Foundations & Sculpture at Michigan State University.

 

Admission: Free

Gallery Hours: Monday-Friday, 8 am-5 pm

 

A weeknight or daytime permit is now required after 5:00 pm on weekdays. No permit is required from 5:00 pm Friday through 7:30 am Monday. A $1.00 one-night pass is available in selected lots. More information can be found HERE.

 

For more information, please contact: Annette Lawrence, annettel@unc.edu

title: Second Annual Institute on Spirituality: Building Interfaith Community: Dialogue and Action for Social Change
location: UNC School of Social Work, Tate-Turner-Kuralt Auditorium
description:
Faith communities, spiritual traditions and the helping professions all carry powerful resources for connection, meaning and community. At a time when many people feel isolated, overwhelmed or divided by political, social and religious conflict, this institute will explore how practitioners, community leaders and faith-based organizations can move from shared values to collective action.

The UNC School of Social Work is hosting its second annual institute on spirituality for public health professionals, scholars and practitioners on Friday, Oct. 9.

“Building Interfaith Community: Dialogue and Action for Social Change” will feature a keynote address from Pamela Ayo Yetunde, co-founder of Buddhist Justice Reporter and the Year of the Black Woman Spiritual Direction program, as well as the author of several books.

The institute will bring together social workers, mental health providers, chaplains, clergy, spiritual care providers, public health professionals, students and community leaders to examine common threads across spiritual and religious traditions: connection to something beyond the self, connection to other people and responsibility to the wider community.

title: Play the Cyber Bowl
description:
It's time to play the third annual Cyber Bowl, a month-long competition to determine which North Carolina university is the most cyber savvy. 

 

All October long, students, faculty and staff can log into the Cyber Bowl website and take a short cybersecurity quiz. Each completed quiz earns a point for Carolina.

 

UNC-Chapel Hill faces off against nine other North Carolina universities with a lot to prove and two wins to defend. In the inaugural Cyber Bowl, Carolina won the championship by garnering the largest participation by percentage. Last year, Carolina fielded the most players — almost 2,000 — of any school.

 

The Cyber Bowl is sponsored by Information Technology Services and the Information Security Office as part of National Cybersecurity Awareness Month.

title: B19 Ride, 50+ miles, 19-20 mph
description:
Carolina Tarwheels Cycling Club
Goal is a brisk **group** ride, maintaining an organized pace line, going easy on the climbs and speeding up on the descents and communicating potential hazards to the group.

Route: Route to be published by Thursday @ 8 PM

Your responsibility as part of the group is to RSVP and supply your own cue sheet or download the GPS file. **RSVP is required.** If you plan to join the ride in progress, leave a comment below on where we can expect to meet you.

**NOTE!**
This is NOT a no-drop ride. All riders are expected to be skilled and experienced in SAFE pace line riding and capable of maintaining an average pace of 19-20 mph. **The ride is limited to 20 riders.** We may split the group into two smaller groups, depending on how many show up.

It is Tarwheels policy for all riders to sign the ride waiver before coming out to the ride.

\*\*\* WAIVER \*\*\* [http://tarwheels.net/ewaiver](http://tarwheels.net/ewaiver)

title: Roots of Discovery: Sands of Knowledge
location: Downtown Raleigh, 11 West Jones Street, Raleigh, NC, 27601, United States
description:
Journey through the rich cultures of the Muslim world and discover an extraordinary legacy of curiosity, creativity and innovation. Explore how scholars, artists and thinkers preserved ancient knowledge, transformed it through new discoveries, and shared ideas that would influence Europe and help shape our modern understanding of mathematics, astronomy, medicine, art, architecture and the natural world. 
Presentations

12:30 – 1pm, SECU Daily Planet Theater
Hearts, Minds, and Healing: How Caring for Others Connects Us All
Caring for others is rarely a one-way exchange; what we extend to others returns to shape us. This session transitions between the heart and the mind. It brings the compassion and service at the center of Islamic tradition into conversation with empathy and self-awareness, the cornerstones of emotional intelligence, and asks how each becomes a form of healing. What emerges is a picture of what encourages individuals make a meaning of their own stories, allows them to feel seen and heard. Recognition, in turn, is what binds a community together 
About the speaker
Fatma Wasel was born in Kuwait, raised in Yemen, and has Egyptian roots. She holds a Doctorate in Executive Leadership focused on emotional intelligence and cross-cultural integration. A U.S. State Department alumna, educator, trainer, activist, and linguist, she has worked across government, nonprofit, and private sectors nationally and internationally. 

1 – 1:30pm, SECU Daily Planet Theater
Healing and Discovery: The Muslim Legacy in Medicine and Engineering
From Al-Zahrawi, the father of modern surgery whose surgical texts shaped European medicine for centuries, to Al-Jazari’s ingenious mechanical inventions, this talk explores the golden age of Muslim scientific achievement in medicine and engineering. Discover how scholars across the Islamic world advanced surgery, pharmacology, and mechanical design in ways that continue to influence science today. 
About the speaker
Mohsen Zakaib is a physician-in-training with a multidisciplinary background in nuclear engineering, business, and Islamic studies. He holds bachelor’s and master’s degrees in Nuclear Engineering, an MBA, and a bachelor’s in Islamic Studies. Mohsen serves as Director of Development at the Lighthouse Project and co-founded RISE at the Islamic Association of Raleigh. 
Activities
Nature Research Center Lobby
Creatures beyond the Sand: Wildlife Across a Continent 
NC Museum of Natural Sciences
Journey beyond the desert and discover the incredible diversity of animals found across Africa and its surrounding islands. Meet fascinating creatures and explore the unique adaptations that help them thrive in habitats from forests and wetlands to grasslands and beyond. 
Mapping the Heavens: Stars, Time & Discovery
Artist Ummah
Look to the skies and discover how Muslim scholars mapped the stars, measured time and expanded our understanding of the universe. 
Healing Through Knowledge: The Roots of Medicine
Artist Ummah
Discover how Muslim physicians studied the human body, advanced medical treatments and preserved knowledge that helped shape modern medicine. 
The Living Lineage: A Journey into the Muslim Arts 
Artist Ummah
Journey through timeless traditions of calligraphy, geometry, tezhip, ebru, and other contemporary art forms inspired by the classical Muslim arts. Discover how artists across North Carolina are reimagining these rich traditions while honoring their heritage and helping keep these beautiful art forms alive for generations to come. 
Interactive Arabic Calligraphy Demonstration 
Artist Ummah
Experience a live Arabic calligraphy demonstration with local artist, who will showcase the art of Arabic lettering and write visitors´names in Arabic. 
Sips of History: Coffee, Tea & Tradition  
Artist Ummah
Explore the fascinating journey of coffee from its roots in the Muslim world, where it was cultivated, brewed, and celebrated as part of social and intellectual life.  
A Cup of Connection 
Salt & Cheeni 
Enjoy a complimentary sample of freshly brewed coffee with Salt & Cheeni! Discover how the right grind and brewing method bring out the best in every bean, and explore how coffee is more than just a drink—it’s conversation, connection, and comfort in a cup.

title: Open Studio: Glass & Other
location: Fusion Gallery, 321 W Main St, Durham, 27701, United States
description:
Drop in and create on your own terms! Your Open Studio Day Pass gives you access to Fusion Gallery’s shared studio space from 1:00 PM–7:00 PM on your selected day. Come in anytime after 1:00 PM and stay as late as 7:00 PM. 
Use our studio space and tools or bring your own project to work on; perfect for artists who don’t have a home studio or simply want dedicated time and space to make. Personal cubbies are also available to store works-in-progress between visits. 
Online registration or sign-up via email is required before coming in. Drop-ins are not permitted at this time. If you’d like to come in at a time you don’t see available online, email us at info@fusionnc.com. 
How Open Studio Works
Open Studio is self-guided and does not include instruction. You should already have the skills needed to safely work in your chosen medium. It’s also a great opportunity to finish projects started during a Fusion class. 
Your Day Pass includes access to our shared workspace, tools, equipment, and currently available non-consumable materials. Consumable and specialty materials are charged separately based on usage. 
Stained & Fused Glass
Prior stained or fused glass experience is required to use our glass tools. Taking a basics or beginner class at Fusion is recommended, but previous instruction at Carolina Stained Glass or Say It With Glass is also accepted. 
• Glass, solder, foil, and frit: $35/lb
• Bringing your own stained glass? Foil and solder use: $6
• Paper stained glass patterns: Free
• Vinyl-cut patterns: $3 each
• An assortment of stained glass patterns is available for studio use
• Kiln firings are handled by Fusion staff only 
Silver Clay
Prior silver clay experience is required to use silver clay tools. Taking a beginner class at Fusion is recommended before using the studio independently. 
• Silver clay: $7/gram prior to firing
• Firing of your completed piece is included and will be completed at the convenience of Fusion studio staff
• Guests may not fire their own pieces without prior authorization from Fusion’s owners 
Drawing & Painting
No prior class or experience is required for drawing or painting. Your Open Studio fee includes access to currently available shared drawing and painting materials. 
Please Note
• Day Pass access is valid 1:00 PM–7:00 PM on your selected date only
• Online or email registration is required before arriving—no walk-ins
• Open Studio is self-guided and does not include instruction
• Some specialty tools, equipment, or processes may require prior approval or demonstrated experience
• Guests are responsible for cleaning their workspace and helping maintain a respectful shared environment
• Misuse of the space, tools, or equipment or failure to follow studio guidelines may result in removal from the studio without refund

title: Climate Up Close
location: Nature Research Center, 121 West Jones Street, Raleigh, NC, 27601, United States
description:
Meet a panel of climate scientists and put your questions to them yourself.
Join us for a presentation and Q&A with climate scientists from Climate Up Close in the SECU Daily Planet Theater. 
Climate Up Close works to inform and elevate the national conversation on climate change by explaining the scientific consensus clearly, without partisanship or policy prescriptions. They challenge both denialism and fatalism—the opposing extremes that too often distort climate discourse. Their team of working climate scientists travels to communities across the country so that people can see the evidence for themselves and put their questions directly to researchers. Each event features a 45-minute talk that maps the landscape of climate knowledge, sorting impacts like heat waves, sea level rise, and hurricanes along a spectrum from well understood to genuinely uncertain. Following the talk, there is an extended Q&A and time to chat with the scientists one-on-one. 
Our presenters 
Current scientist members include Dr. Nadir Jeevanjee (NOAA), Dr. Aaron Match (Cornell University), Dr. Nathaniel Tarshish (Harvard University), and Dr. Andrew Williams (UC San Diego).

description:
FEATURING

TALsounds

Natalie Chami (TALsounds) is a Canadian-born Lebanese American musician and educator based in Alexandria, VA. Known for her work in drone, ambient, and improvisational music, she blends vintage analog synthesizers, operatic vocals, and immersive atmospheres into distinctive sound worlds. Chami has released music on Ba Da Bing, NNA Tapes, and Hausu Mountain, toured across the U.S., Canada, and Europe, and received coverage from Pitchfork, The Fader, The Washington Post, and The Chicago Tribune. Her latest album, Shift (2023), departs from her warm analog palette and explores FM and digital synthesis, featuring contributions from SWANA women in production, art, and photography. 

Chami was founding Vocal Chair at The Chicago High School for the Arts (2009–2021), developing the voice department and trauma-informed, anti-racist curriculum. She also leads workshops at universities, scores films, creates sound installations, and is the Category Content Specialist for Synthesizers at KORG USA. In 2025, she was invited to serve on Experimental Sound Studio’s first-ever Artist Advisory Council, supporting the development of new online programming for artists in electronic and sound art.

title: Be and Feel Good Enough to End Anxiety, Struggle, and Exhaustion
description:
Raleigh & Triangle Activities Meetup Group
A strange thing happens when perfectly good people ponder a lie: they start imagining that they’re not good enough, until they actually become not good enough. They can feel that something is wrong, but they think that people are the problem while the false thinking is true. Of course that’s the point, because the lies must cover up for not being good enough while human beings were always better than they ever knew. Trying to win at this rigged losing game is now causing epidemic anxiety, struggle and exhaustion. Many become so desperate to survive on lies that they become their own lie. They ignore the most basic emotional facts while spreading conspiracy theories to play hero for the paranoid. Insecure narcissists and demagogues pretend to be powerful by instinctively misleading everyone to react for or against them, with either way feeding the lies. The truth is increasingly obvious yet remains so unfamiliar and unpopular that many will ignore their own answers to the bitter end. Forget what’s out there; you must be and feel good enough inside to remember what’s true for you.

Join us this Sunday Oct 11, 2026 for a free heart-and-mind opening talk on what it means to really know that you’re always good enough. I’ve been training my whole life with my spirit guides to help humanity through the transition today, and I’m still amazed at what it feels like to experience the beauty of the human potential. Life isn’t hard; that was a lie. Nothing is ever lost, neither in time nor space; those were more lies. Hard work and struggle aren’t noble or effective, they only bring more hard work and struggle. Nobody ever changes anyone or anything else, so to try is the cause of endless stress and distress. Just by discovering and choosing what’s true for you, you will change automatically and enter a new better world. Everyone is continually creating their own next future timeline, so predicting and planning from the past cannot work. You’re always predestined to live happily ever after. You just have to learn how to let it be true.

We’ll see how belief systems work to create the layers of reality experience that can seem so real until they reach a dead end. Stop trying to fix what’s always been broken. Understand that you already have what always works. You’ll learn how the spirit human partnership within you functions most beautifully to rescue yourself and show the way home. Your human emotions are the secret treasure or curse, as you choose to either reactively feed the reality that’s controlling you, or responsively grow your spiritual abilities to live your own destiny. You’ll learn how to escape the traps of anxiety, panic, and compulsions of low self-esteem like procrastination and addictive pleasures. The combination of human and spiritual perspectives is needed to catch traumatic lies and replace them with deeper solutions. We’ll conclude with a guided meditation to let your soul family and friends lead you into the plans you already made at higher levels for your own best happiness.

Welcome! Our Inner Selves Mastery spiritual support group is free online every Sunday 11am-1:30pm EST, with the last half hour for a guided meditation. You can signup here for this meeting, check [www.meetup.com/Inner-Selves-for-Outer-Mastery](http://www.meetup.com/Inner-Selves-for-Outer-Mastery) for all events, and visit our landing page at [www.signupism.com](http://www.signupism.com) for newsletter, YouTube channel, and more.

WHAT TO EXPECT: Meetings are online with zoom, link posted by day of meeting. Each week Spirit gives me a theme to explore for loving empowerment and reality creation. I gather teachings from my spiritual psychology system and learn more throughout the week until I write a channeled manifesto to focus the meeting. Our format works great with 4 parts: intro, check-ins, main talk, and guided meditation to put ideas into practice.

BACKGROUND: My name is Carl, I’m a spiritual teacher and life coach. My Spirit team has guided me for over 30 years to develop a system for personal evolution called Inner Selves Mastery, which shows how the many parts of You can work better with the Source to live in a loving Universe. I’ve been leading groups for over 25 years, and since the massive shifts of 2020 offering as much support as I can.

Best wishes,
Carl Johann Schroeder

title: University Worship
location: Duke Chapel
description:
Join us in worship that offers stirring preaching, inspiring sacred music, and faithful prayer. Held year-round amid the beautiful, soaring architecture of Duke Chapel, this interdenominational Christian service is characterized by vibrant faith, intellectual depth, diverse cultural expressions, and a welcoming community.

To attend a service, navigate to 125 Science Drive, Durham, NC. Parking is available at that address in the Bryan Center Garage with ADA parking in the adjacent surface lot. Parking in the garage is free on Sunday until 2:00 p.m. when using the standard ticket issued upon entering the garage. Regular attendees of the service are encouraged to receive a pass for free parking on Sunday mornings at the visitor desk inside the Chapel.

Resources for the service:
* Make an offering online: https://chapel.duke.edu/offering
* View an online version of the hymnal here: https://hymnary.org/hymnal/UMH

A national leader in the theological study of the art of preaching, Chapel Dean Luke A. Powery preaches regularly at this service, along with a rotation of other Chapel ministers and renowned guest preachers. The acclaimed Duke Chapel Choir and Chapel organists lead the music, supplemented by student chamber groups, professional instrumentalists, and visiting artists.

Services are streamed live on YouTube and broadcast live on channel 12 of the Duke Hospital TV system and on the radio on 620 AM WDNC. Subscribe to the Duke Chapel Sermons podcast on Spotify or Apple Podcasts. Find an archive of Chapel sermons on our website and a more extensive digital archive in the Duke Chapel Recordings collection on the Duke Libraries website.

For a listing of Christian education offerings held before the service, see the Duke Chapel website calendar.

title: Adrián Uribe: 50 y Pico Tour
location: DPAC Presented by First Horizon, 123 Vivian St / William V. "Bill" Bell Way, Durham, 27701
description:
Celebrating Uribe’s remarkable 35-year career, the special production will see him once again bring to life beloved characters such as El Vítor, Carmelo, Poncho Aurelio, and Serapio, whose enduring popularity has established him as one of the most celebrated comedians of his generation. Blending nostalgia, comedy, improvisation, and brand-new stories, 50 y Pico Tour invites audiences to reconnect with these iconic characters while celebrating the lasting bond Uribe has built with generations of fans. 
“I’ve missed touring the U.S. with my own show because the love from the Latino community here is truly unmatched,” Uribe shared. 
Throughout his career, Uribe has starred in some of Mexico’s most successful television productions, including La Hora Pico, Mi Corazón es Tuyo, Nosotros los Guapos, ¿Quién es la Máscara?, and De Noche… Pero Sin Sueño. Beyond television, he has also enjoyed success in film, voice acting, and theater, as well as with hit live tours such as Imparables, EnParejados, and ChavoRucos, all of which have played to sold-out audiences across Mexico and the United States. 
Celebrando 35 años de trayectoria, este espectáculo marca el esperado reencuentro de Adrián Uribe con el público a través de entrañables personajes como El Vítor, Carmelo, Poncho Aurelio y Serapio, quienes lo han consolidado como uno de los comediantes más importantes de su generación. Combinando nostalgia, humor, improvisación y nuevas historias, 50 y Pico Tour invita al público a reencontrarse con estos personajes icónicos mientras celebra el vínculo que Uribe ha construido con generaciones de seguidores. 
“He extrañado hacer gira por Estados Unidos con mi propio show porque el amor de la comunidad latina aquí no tiene comparación”, compartió Uribe. 
A lo largo de su carrera, Uribe ha protagonizado algunos de los proyectos más exitosos de la televisión mexicana, entre ellos La Hora Pico, Mi Corazón es Tuyo, Nosotros los Guapos, ¿Quién es la Máscara? y De Noche… Pero Sin Sueño. Además, ha destacado en el cine, el doblaje y el teatro, así como en giras de gran éxito como Imparables, EnParejados y ChavoRucos, con las que agotó localidades tanto en México como en Estados Unidos.

title: John and June Allcott Gallery: Michelle Inez Hinojosa and Barbara Pearsall
location: Hanes Art Center, John and June Allcott Gallery
description:
Art and Art History

Under the Tent: Whirling & Flickering

August 20-October 15, 2026

Reception: August 20, 5-7 pm

 

Drawn together in graduate school by their mutual love of experimentation and play, Michelle Inez Hinojosa and Barbara Pearsall have built a collaborative practice around analogue animation and vibrant abstraction. Together, their work explores optical toys, immersive installations, and movement. Under the Tent: Whirling & Flickering features kaleidoscopic imagery, flickering abstractions, projection mapping, a hidden trapdoor, and hand-cranked wheels that transform what viewers see. After searching for the perfect venue, they are thrilled to bring their collaborative installation to UNC. Their first public artwork, Turnabout Folly, will debut in Lansing, Michigan in Fall 2026.

 

Michelle Hinojosa works at the intersection of painting, poetry, and fiber art, where she considers memory, intergenerational trauma, and migration. Born in central Texas, by way of the fields of California and Northern Mexico, Michelle uplifts traditions of making that have provided much-needed stability to a family displaced. Michelle Hinojosa is an Assistant Professor of Art at Pennsylvania State University.

 

Barbara Pearsall is an artist and educator based in Michigan. Her art practice is attentive to how deviation from material conventions can subvert or metamorphose the role of institutions, where her philosophical and political concerns manifest through material explorations of the built environment. Her pieces seek to create illusory and unusual architectural conditions as a form of resistance, interrupting real-world functionality to allow for alternative systems of order. She is an Assistant Professor of Foundations & Sculpture at Michigan State University.

 

Admission: Free

Gallery Hours: Monday-Friday, 8 am-5 pm

 

A weeknight or daytime permit is now required after 5:00 pm on weekdays. No permit is required from 5:00 pm Friday through 7:30 am Monday. A $1.00 one-night pass is available in selected lots. More information can be found HERE.

 

For more information, please contact: Annette Lawrence, annettel@unc.edu

description:
The 2026 Duke-ORNL Workshop on Advanced Microscopy and Data-Driven Materials Science will be held at Duke University on October 12-13, 2026. The workshop will bring together leading researchers, industry experts, and emerging scholars to explore the latest advances in electron microscopy, AI-enabled data analysis, and data-driven materials discovery.

The program will showcase cutting-edge characterization techniques and computational approaches for next-generation energy and quantum materials, including batteries, two-dimensional materials, and complex interfaces. By connecting fundamental research with industrial applications, the workshop will foster collaborations among academia, national laboratories, and industry while engaging regional industry partners.

Students and postdoctoral researchers are especially encouraged to participate. The workshop will feature networking opportunities, career development activities, and a poster session with awards recognizing outstanding student and postdoctoral presentations.

By fostering interdisciplinary dialogue, the workshop aims to identify new research opportunities and support the development of the next-generation materials science workforce.

title: Bowditch Bottoms Wetland Planting (Burnsville)
description:
Join the North Carolina Wildlife Federation, Southern Appalachian Highlands Conservancy, and Wildbud Natives for a wetland planting workday at Bowditch Bottoms in Yancey County. Bowditch Bottoms is a 87-acre property that contains important soils, farmland, undeveloped forested and non-forested habitat for wildlife, headwaters to the South Toe River, and intact wetland and riparian corridors. It is visible from the Mount Mitchell Scenic Byway and several higher-elevation vantage points in the Black Mountains and the Highlands of the Roan. 
NCWF, SAHC, conservation professionals alongside volunteers have worked together at Bowditch Bottoms to restore habitat, increase biodiversity, and serve as a model for active stewardship. Together on the property through multiple workdays we have removed Helene debris, controlled non-native invasive plant species, hosted a hands-on forestry workshop with EcoForesters, planted over a thousand livestakes, and engaged the local community with a grassroots conservation project. 
Join us to continue the work! During this workday, we’ll be planting over 2 thousand wetland species including swamp milkweed, pale jewelweed, bushy bluestem, and more. Bring some snacks and we’ll see you there!

title: University Day in Wilson Library
location: Wilson Library
description:
On October 12, in commemoration of University Day, Wilson Library will host a Carolina History Trivia event and provide a rare opportunity to view two of the oldest and most significant items from the university history collections.

From 11:00-1:00 p.m. on October 12, the University Archives will host Carolina History Trivia in front of Wilson Library. Students and others are encouraged to drop by and test their knowledge on the history of UNC-Chapel Hill. Participants will compete head-to-head and have an opportunity to win prizes.

The library will also feature a one-day-only display of two unique artifacts:

The original plaque placed into the cornerstone of Old East on October 12, 1793. This artifact has a direct tie to the ceremony held to begin construction for the university. It also has a fascinating history, disappearing from campus for more than 40 years before being discovered at a foundry in Tennessee and returned to Chapel Hill in 1916. Learn more: https://www.unc.edu/posts/2025/10/03/the-old-east-plaque-once-mysteriously-disappeared/
 
A diploma from UNC’s first commencement, 1798. After opening in 1795, Carolina held its first commencement in July 1798. Seven students earned degrees that day, including Hinton James, the first student to attend the university. The diploma on display was awarded to Adam Springs, a student from Mecklenburg County who was part of the first graduating class. It is handwritten on parchment and signed by several of the early trustees, including William Richardson Davie.


These artifacts will be on exhibit in the Wilson Library main lobby from 9:30-4:30 p.m. on October 12.

title: Mesh-LLM & Trusting a Stranger's Machine, Part 2: Evidence You Can Check
description:
All Things AI (Live)
When a stranger's machine serves an AI request, how can the requester check what happened? We'll show mesh-llm's Evidence plugin recording signed, hash-chained evidence on each node and sending each side's signed record to the other.

A demo build will show both-sides confirmation and a paid Lightning exchange; we'll label the build and distinguish it from a released version. I'll show a TRACE record alongside the exchange capsule to explain what additional runtime evidence, including hardware evidence when available, can establish. We'll also show the limits: the plugin's node keys are self-attested, and its referee applies once mesh-llm marks twins.

title: Spill the Tea: An LGBTQ+ Spooky Season Mixer 👻🌈
description:
Discover Durham Together
Spooky season is here, and we’re brewing up something a little different. 👻

Join Triangle Third Place and Discover Durham Together at Drink a Bull in Durham for an LGBTQ+ mixer filled with tea, cocktails, mocktails, new connections, and just enough Halloween chaos.

Come in costume, add a little spooky flair, or just show up as yourself... there is no requirement.

🧪 Potion Pairing

When you arrive, you’ll receive half of a mysterious potion pairing. Somewhere in the room, another person has your match. Find them, introduce yourselves, and claim a jelly bracelet for completing each pairing.

Then grab another "potion" and do it again.

Collect bracelets throughout the night as you meet new people, with absolutely no pressure for those connections to be romantic. Friendship, community, flirting, networking, finding your future karaoke duo… it all counts.

If you have a sleeve of bracelets by the end of the night, just know you're a winner and better than everyone else.

☕ Spill the Tea

Who doesn't like some Tea? We’ll also have an anonymous Spill the Tea jar circulating throughout the evening.

Drop in a confession, unpopular opinion, ridiculous dating story, queer awakening, Halloween hot take, or harmless secret. Throughout the night, we’ll pull a few out and expose them.

No names. No judgment. Potentially a little chaos.

🐂 Drink a Bull

Drink a Bull serves both specialty teas and alcoholic beverages, so whether your potion of choice is boozy, caffeinated, or completely alcohol-free, there’s something for you.

Come meet people. Collect some bracelets. Spill a little tea. Maybe cast a spell or two.

title: Close Up Foundation Next Gen - A DAY OF DELIBERATIVE DIALOGUE
location: None
description:
On October 13, 2026, Close Up will lead a regional deliberation at Duke University. This event is one of six regional deliberations taking place in 2026-27 across the country as part of NextGen Roundtable: America 250, a growing initiative to honor the Semiquincentennial of the United States. Through civil discourse, we aim to empower students to engage in meaningful dialogue, listen with empathy, and express their ideas with clarity and confidence.


This NextGen Roundtable regional deliberation will convene up to 250 high school students from public, charter, private, and independent schools in the area
who represent a cross-section of backgrounds and perspectives. Students will deliberate on economic policy issues in small groups moderated by neutral
facilitators, weigh diverse perspectives from their peers and a panel of policy experts, and craft vision statements for making an impact in their community.
All participating students will receive Close Up's Deliberative Dialogue Badge.

As students deliberate, accompanying educators will take part in a Close Up-led professional development workshop around deliberative dialogue and
political values, including an introduction to Close Up's free, four-week curricular unit, "Cornerstones of American Democracy," about how our country's
core political values regularly come into tension. Following the PD session, educators will earn continuing education units for applying what they learn in
their classrooms.

title: John and June Allcott Gallery: Michelle Inez Hinojosa and Barbara Pearsall
location: Hanes Art Center, John and June Allcott Gallery
description:
Art and Art History

Under the Tent: Whirling & Flickering

August 20-October 15, 2026

Reception: August 20, 5-7 pm

 

Drawn together in graduate school by their mutual love of experimentation and play, Michelle Inez Hinojosa and Barbara Pearsall have built a collaborative practice around analogue animation and vibrant abstraction. Together, their work explores optical toys, immersive installations, and movement. Under the Tent: Whirling & Flickering features kaleidoscopic imagery, flickering abstractions, projection mapping, a hidden trapdoor, and hand-cranked wheels that transform what viewers see. After searching for the perfect venue, they are thrilled to bring their collaborative installation to UNC. Their first public artwork, Turnabout Folly, will debut in Lansing, Michigan in Fall 2026.

 

Michelle Hinojosa works at the intersection of painting, poetry, and fiber art, where she considers memory, intergenerational trauma, and migration. Born in central Texas, by way of the fields of California and Northern Mexico, Michelle uplifts traditions of making that have provided much-needed stability to a family displaced. Michelle Hinojosa is an Assistant Professor of Art at Pennsylvania State University.

 

Barbara Pearsall is an artist and educator based in Michigan. Her art practice is attentive to how deviation from material conventions can subvert or metamorphose the role of institutions, where her philosophical and political concerns manifest through material explorations of the built environment. Her pieces seek to create illusory and unusual architectural conditions as a form of resistance, interrupting real-world functionality to allow for alternative systems of order. She is an Assistant Professor of Foundations & Sculpture at Michigan State University.

 

Admission: Free

Gallery Hours: Monday-Friday, 8 am-5 pm

 

A weeknight or daytime permit is now required after 5:00 pm on weekdays. No permit is required from 5:00 pm Friday through 7:30 am Monday. A $1.00 one-night pass is available in selected lots. More information can be found HERE.

 

For more information, please contact: Annette Lawrence, annettel@unc.edu

title: Durham Social Hack Night
description:
Triangle Developers
Hey tech folks, come out and hang at Hi-Wire starting at 6pm! Hack Night is meant to be a social evening for folks in tech. It's less about networking and more about community.

**Look for the Hack Night tabletop sign** and nerds wearing name tags to find us. If the weather is nice, we'll probably be outside.

Help folks feel welcome by using the **"Pac Man Rule"** \- when standing with a group of people \(usually in a circle\)\, leave some space open so that another person can easily join\.

See our [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/TriangleDevsSlack/policies/blob/master/code-of-conduct.md). To summarize: be nice or leave. No tolerance for harassment or oppression. In addition, since alcohol is present at these events, please be mindful of your consumption and respect other people's choices on whether or not to consume.

**FAQs**
*Do folks hack at Hack Night? Should I bring my computer?*
This is more of a night for hackers than an actual hack night. You're welcome to bring a laptop, but most people will only be socializing.

*What are the beverage options? Are there any non-alcoholic drinks?*
Hi-Wire Brewing offers many types of beers including a few non-alcoholic options plus wine and some liquor. They usually have a happy hour special on the first few beers on the menu. In the same complex are Cugino Forno which has additional drink options, and Two Roosters which has excellent ice cream.

*Are there any drink specials?*
If Hack Night is on a Tuesday, Hi-Wire usually has $5 pints for their flagship beers. Look for the list at the counter.

*Do people eat snacks/dinner during the meetup?*
Sometimes folks will order a pizza or salad from Cugino Forno. I sometimes grab an ice cream from Two Roosters across the way. Most people eat before or after but it's no big deal - whatever you prefer and are most comfortable with.

*How can I connect with the developer community?*
Go to [triangledevelopers.com](https://triangledevelopers.com/) to find the Discord and Slack info.

title: Renée Fleming in Recital: ‘Voice of Nature: The Anthropocene’
location: Memorial Hall
description:
When was the last time a performance changed the way you looked at the world around you? 

Voice of Nature: the Anthropocene is an exploration of one of the defining issues of our time—environmental change—through music and imagery. It invites us to consider the beauty and fragility of the natural world and our relationship to it.

Performed by acclaimed soprano Renée Fleming, the program pairs classical songs and contemporary works with an original film created in partnership with the National Geographic Society. The experience is both intimate and expansive, sharing landscapes of breathtaking beauty alongside acute reminders of their vulnerability.

 

At a moment when environmental change increasingly shapes everyday life, Voice of Nature reminds us that these challenges are not just scientific or political; they are deeply personal. It is an invitation to consider how rapidly the natural world is changing while reflecting on how much we rely on its constancy for solace, inspiration, and a sense of connection to something larger than ourselves.

title: John and June Allcott Gallery: Michelle Inez Hinojosa and Barbara Pearsall
location: Hanes Art Center, John and June Allcott Gallery
description:
Art and Art History

Under the Tent: Whirling & Flickering

August 20-October 15, 2026

Reception: August 20, 5-7 pm

 

Drawn together in graduate school by their mutual love of experimentation and play, Michelle Inez Hinojosa and Barbara Pearsall have built a collaborative practice around analogue animation and vibrant abstraction. Together, their work explores optical toys, immersive installations, and movement. Under the Tent: Whirling & Flickering features kaleidoscopic imagery, flickering abstractions, projection mapping, a hidden trapdoor, and hand-cranked wheels that transform what viewers see. After searching for the perfect venue, they are thrilled to bring their collaborative installation to UNC. Their first public artwork, Turnabout Folly, will debut in Lansing, Michigan in Fall 2026.

 

Michelle Hinojosa works at the intersection of painting, poetry, and fiber art, where she considers memory, intergenerational trauma, and migration. Born in central Texas, by way of the fields of California and Northern Mexico, Michelle uplifts traditions of making that have provided much-needed stability to a family displaced. Michelle Hinojosa is an Assistant Professor of Art at Pennsylvania State University.

 

Barbara Pearsall is an artist and educator based in Michigan. Her art practice is attentive to how deviation from material conventions can subvert or metamorphose the role of institutions, where her philosophical and political concerns manifest through material explorations of the built environment. Her pieces seek to create illusory and unusual architectural conditions as a form of resistance, interrupting real-world functionality to allow for alternative systems of order. She is an Assistant Professor of Foundations & Sculpture at Michigan State University.

 

Admission: Free

Gallery Hours: Monday-Friday, 8 am-5 pm

 

A weeknight or daytime permit is now required after 5:00 pm on weekdays. No permit is required from 5:00 pm Friday through 7:30 am Monday. A $1.00 one-night pass is available in selected lots. More information can be found HERE.

title: Oct 14 - Advances in AI at SDSU
description:
Raleigh AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join our virtual meetup to hear talks from AI researchers at San Diego State University.

**Date, Time Location**

Oct 14, 2026
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/advances-in-ai-at-sdsu-october-14-2026)**

**Agent as Policy for Robotic Manipulation**

This talk will introduces how a general-purpose agent can directly drive a physical robot throughout task execution without any task-specific or environment-specific training. We introduce Agent as Policy (AGP), which places task planning and execution under the agent’s control.

*About the Speaker*

[Xiaobai Liu](https://www.linkedin.com/in/xiaobai-liu-33598336/) is a Professor of Computer Science at San Diego State University (SDSU), where he directs the Machine Vision and Perception Lab. Prior to joining SDSU in 2015, he conducted research and taught at UCLA.

**Grounding Multimodal Open-World Learning for Physical AI**

Physical AI systems such as robots, unmanned vehicles, and embodied agents must perceive and reason about a world that is dynamic, unstructured, and rarely matches their training distribution. Yet most multimodal models remain brittle when confronted with novel objects, unseen conditions, and a messy unstructured environment.

This talk develops how grounding perception across modalities and environments can make open-world learning more robust for physically situated systems. Drawing on our recent work, I will highlight the core challenges of multimodal open-world learning including out-of-distribution detection, distribution shift generalization, and cascaded semantic grounding and point toward multimodal systems that stay reliable when deployed in the unpredictable open world.

*About the Speakers*

[Salimeh Sekeh](https://www.linkedin.com/in/salimeh-sekeh-65473344/) is an Associate Professor of Computer Science at San Diego State University (SDSU), where she directs the Sekeh Laboratory. Her recognition includes an NSF CAREER Award and a Cisco research gift (both 2022), and the Maine College of Engineering and Computing Early Career Research Award (2023), along with multiple industry and federal research awards.

[Mary Wisell ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mary-isabelle-wisell/)is a second-year PhD student in the Sekeh Lab and leads the lab's work on environment-aware OOD detection and cascaded failure analysis for multimodal intelligence with several publications in top-tier Machine Learning and computer vision conferences.

**Model-Free, Position-Free Signal Source Seeking Using Unmanned Maritime Systems**

Long-range signal source detection in open-world environments presents a significant challenge, mainly due to the detrimental effects of the environment on signals propagation paths and presence of extraneous signal sources. While distributed static sensing systems are often employed, achieving scalability and comprehensive coverage across expansive areas is cost-prohibitive.

One affordable solution involves using low-cost autonomous unmanned vehicles (AUVs) that can leverage their mobility and actively explore the environment using extremum seeking control (ESC) algorithms. This talk presents novel ESC approaches to steer AUVs to sources of interest in an a priori unknown, highly non-convex map.

*About the Speaker*

[Zahra Nili Ahmadabadi](https://www.linkedin.com/in/zahra-nili-ahmadabadi-phd-29113171) is Associate Professor with the Mechanical Engineering Department at San Diego State University (SDSU). She is a recipient of the ASME rising star award and ARO Early career award.

Look closely at these structures under a microscope, then venture outside to meet specimens living in the garden. title: Renée Fleming Music & Mind
location: Memorial Hall
description:
What happens in your brain when music moves you to tears? What can we advance in neuroscience when a researcher asks why a melody can unlock a memory, ease anxiety, or help a patient heal? 

 

For years, Renée Fleming has worked alongside physicians and researchers to better understand the profound relationship between music and human health. In this conversation, presented in partnership with the UNC School of Medicine and moderated by arts and culture journalist Liza Roberts, Fleming and UNC neuroscientists and practitioners explore how the arts are informing cutting-edge developments and reshaping clinical practice.

 

The discussion moves beyond theory and into applications that touch everyday life: how creative experiences matter to your well-being, and how scientists are establishing important roles for the arts in healing, connection, and human flourishing.

 

This is a rare opportunity to hear artists, scientists, and medical professionals share the same stage and to discover how one of humanity’s oldest forms of expression is shaping the future of health care.

 

Please note: Renée Fleming will not be performing during this program. Join us for her separately-ticketed performance on October 13.

 

Student tickets always $11. Eligible for CLE. Find out more and buy tickets at: https://carolinaperformingarts.org/events/musicmind/

Please join our virtual welcome session with this link

Are you a young person between 13 and 25 years old who is interested in taking action around preventing gun violence? Join us for our Team ENOUGH welcome session to learn more about the different ways you can engage. 

Team ENOUGH is a youth-led program whose mission is to educate young voices about gun violence and mobilize them to take meaningful action against it. Supported by Brady United, we harness the expertise and experience of today’s youth to advance our intersectional work across the country. 

Led by an Executive Council, comprised of students just like us, we believe that diversity is a strength, and that only when everyone has a seat at the table can we build an effective movement to prevent all gun violence in all communities.

For us, preventing gun violence not only requires regulating access to firearms but also addressing how systemic racism and environmental factors cause this form of bloodshed to run especially rampant in communities of color. You cannot talk about gun violence without talking about police brutality, white supremacy, the broken criminal justice system, poverty, homophobia, access to affordable housing, or the often barriers separating disadvantaged populations from physical and mental healthcare. 

So if you share this belief, join us for our Team ENOUGH welcome session and become part of the movement to end gun violence in our lifetime.

title: John and June Allcott Gallery: Michelle Inez Hinojosa and Barbara Pearsall
location: Hanes Art Center, John and June Allcott Gallery
description:
Art and Art History

Under the Tent: Whirling & Flickering

August 20-October 15, 2026

Reception: August 20, 5-7 pm

 

Drawn together in graduate school by their mutual love of experimentation and play, Michelle Inez Hinojosa and Barbara Pearsall have built a collaborative practice around analogue animation and vibrant abstraction. Together, their work explores optical toys, immersive installations, and movement. Under the Tent: Whirling & Flickering features kaleidoscopic imagery, flickering abstractions, projection mapping, a hidden trapdoor, and hand-cranked wheels that transform what viewers see. After searching for the perfect venue, they are thrilled to bring their collaborative installation to UNC. Their first public artwork, Turnabout Folly, will debut in Lansing, Michigan in Fall 2026.

 

Michelle Hinojosa works at the intersection of painting, poetry, and fiber art, where she considers memory, intergenerational trauma, and migration. Born in central Texas, by way of the fields of California and Northern Mexico, Michelle uplifts traditions of making that have provided much-needed stability to a family displaced. Michelle Hinojosa is an Assistant Professor of Art at Pennsylvania State University.

 

Barbara Pearsall is an artist and educator based in Michigan. Her art practice is attentive to how deviation from material conventions can subvert or metamorphose the role of institutions, where her philosophical and political concerns manifest through material explorations of the built environment. Her pieces seek to create illusory and unusual architectural conditions as a form of resistance, interrupting real-world functionality to allow for alternative systems of order. She is an Assistant Professor of Foundations & Sculpture at Michigan State University.

 

Admission: Free

Gallery Hours: Monday-Friday, 8 am-5 pm

 

A weeknight or daytime permit is now required after 5:00 pm on weekdays. No permit is required from 5:00 pm Friday through 7:30 am Monday. A $1.00 one-night pass is available in selected lots. More information can be found HERE.

title: Oct 15 - AI, ML, and Computer Vision Meetup
description:
Raleigh AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join our virtual meetup to hear talks from experts on cutting-edge topics across AI, ML, and computer vision.

**Time, Place and Location**

Oct 15, 2026
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/ai-ml-and-computer-vision-meetup-october-15-2026)**

**Testing AI Systems in Production: Data Quality, Drift, and Model Evaluation**

AI systems can pass offline evaluation and still fail in production when real-world data changes, features become stale, labels or feedback signals are incomplete, or model behavior drifts away from expected outcomes. This talk shares practical patterns for testing and evaluating AI systems after deployment, including data quality checks, drift detection, online/offline metric comparison, model monitoring, and rollback analysis.

Using personalization and recommendation systems as examples, we will examine how teams can build evaluation workflows that catch quality issues before users do. Attendees will leave with a practical checklist for making AI-backed systems easier to evaluate, debug, and operate as data changes over time.

*About the Speaker*

[Jayakumar Ramalingam](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jayakumarramalingam) is a Staff Software Engineer and Cloud Architect at SiriusXM with over 16 years of experience building cloud-native platforms, real-time data pipelines, resilient APIs, and AI/ML-enabled applications at production scale.

**Where Should Your Model Live? A Framework for Tiering Computer Vision Deployments**

Where should a computer vision model actually run - on-device, near the edge, or in the cloud? It's a decision that looks simple until requirements like latency, cost, connectivity, and update cadence start pulling in different directions, often revealing themselves only after deployment.

Drawing on hands-on experience developing and deploying CV models across Hailo, Nvidia, Qualcomm and AWS platforms, this talk introduces a practical framework for tiering computer vision deployments based on real project requirements and constraints. Discussion will include what changes at each tier - from development to deployment to monitoring and update strategy - with relevant industry examples.

Attendees will leave with a set of questions or a framework they can use to place their own CV projects into the right tier.

*About the Speaker*

[Ajaykumaar Sivacoumare](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ajay-sa/) is an AI Software Engineer specializing in computer vision and edge AI, with production experience developing and deploying CV models across Nvidia, Hailo, Qualcomm and AWS-based platforms.

**From 2D Slices to 3D Tumors: Lightweight Volumetric Detection Without Heavy 3D Networks**

Slice-wise 2D detectors are fast and scalable, but they struggle to produce reliable 3D bounding boxes from volumetric medical data. This talk presents YOLO-PVC, a lightweight post-processing framework that consolidates slice-wise YOLO detections into coherent 3D bounding boxes using percentile-based geometric aggregation and a minimal MLP calibration module.

This talk demonstrates consistent improvements in volumetric IoU across three liver tumor categories i.e., HCC, CCA, and Mixed, without requiring dense 3D annotations or memory-intensive architectures. The talk covers the clinical motivation, the technical approach, and practical lessons from deploying computer vision on real hospital MRI data.

*About the Speaker*

[Talha Waqas](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mtalha-waqas-255557144/) is a second-year PhD student at ESME Research Lab, Paris and LISSI, Université Paris-Est, working on computer vision applied to medical imaging, with a focus on tumor classification, detection, and segmentation in multi-phase liver MRI.

**The Two-Loop Architecture for Voice AI**

Building responsive voice AI requires balancing latency with intelligence. This talk introduces a practical architecture that separates real-time conversation from asynchronous reasoning, enabling richer interactions without slowing the user experience. The session covers reusable design patterns drawn from production-inspired conversational AI systems.

*About the Speaker*

[Abhinav Tushar](https://lepisma.xyz/wiki/about/) is an ML engineer and researcher specializing in Conversational AI and Speech Technology.

title: The Single Source of Truth: Building Data Foundations for Agentic AI
description:
Data Science Raleigh
Traditional data management was built to give humans consistent, trustworthy records to work from. Agentic AI demands something more dynamic: data that agents can query, reason over, and act on continuously, without waiting for a human to interpret it first. That shift changes what "good" data actually looks like.

This webinar explores how data foundations must evolve to support agentic AI—moving from static, periodically-updated records toward connected, real-time, machine-consumable data. We'll cover what it takes to make data not just accurate, but usable by autonomous systems making decisions at machine speed.

**Key Takeaways:**

1️⃣ **Rethinking "Good" Data:** How agentic AI changes the requirements for data quality and structure.

2️⃣ **Real-Time Unification:** Why static, periodic data processes fall short for continuously acting agents.

3️⃣ **Machine-Readable Trust:** Designing authoritative records that agents can reliably reason over.

4️⃣ **Data Stewardship for Autonomy:** How data ownership roles must adapt as agents become primary data consumers.

**[Register here](https://datasciconnect.com/events/webinars/single-source-of-truth/)**

title: CSA Triangle October Meet-Up | Governing Agentic Work
description:
Cloud Security Alliance Triangle Chapter
**Governing Agentic Work: An Open Architecture for AI Workforce Adoption**

**Summary of Presentation:**
Moving beyond AI chatbots means trusting agents to build applications, reach internal systems, and run repeatable workflows. That trust cannot be granted with a long-lived API key. In this session, Johnnie Tabron draws on Cloudflare's own internal experience and the newly open-sourced Cloudflare OS architecture to show what it actually takes to put agents to work safely.

Attendees will see how organizational context and reusable skills keep agents aligned to established terminology, procedures, and standards, and how a conversation becomes an editable document, a connected application, and a mostly deterministic workflow. They will also learn why capability-based access beats handing credentials to agents and generated code. From there, the talk walks through the governance layer that constrains agent authority, controls where observed data moves, and preserves human accountability, before showing how every step gets centralized oversight and how agents finally ship as isolated, full-stack applications that any organization can deploy and customize in its own Cloudflare account.

Benefits-led but security-focused, the session's central message is that useful enterprise AI demands more than controlling the first model or tool call. Designed for security leaders, architects, cloud and platform engineers, developers, GRC professionals, and AI practitioners, the talk is presented through diagrams, architecture visuals, and interface examples, followed by Q&A.

title: Science Café: Planning for Flooding in the Neuse River Basin
location: Downtown Raleigh, 11 West Jones Street, Raleigh, NC, 27601, United States
description:
Grab a bite from the Daily Planet Café and join host Chris Smith for our monthly Science Café. Gather with other curious minds at this after-hours event for an informal presentation and conversation about current science topics with guest experts. The Daily Planet Café is open 5–8pm with a full menu during the Science Café. 
Join us in-person or watch the livestream on YouTube. 
This month at the Science Café, flood resilience experts will highlight the flooding history of the Neuse River Basin, the solutions proposed to alleviate the flood risks in the area, and how individuals can learn more about flood risk in their own communities. 
In July 2026, the North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ) released the state’s first River Basin Action Strategy (RBAS) for the Neuse River Basin to help mitigate flooding in the region. The Neuse RBAS identified 113 flood resilience actions across the basin, including structural and nonstructural projects such as stormwater improvements, roadway upgrades, nature-based solutions, floodproofing structures, and policy and planning projects. The RBAS was informed by a basin wide vulnerability assessment, community capacity assessment and gap analysis, as well as extensive engagement with local governments, state and federal agencies, nonprofit organizations and other partners throughout the Neuse River Basin. 
Our Experts 
Madison Teeter, CFM Flood Resilience Planner
Suna Rosenberg, Flood Resiliency Program Consultant

title: Pruning with Confidence: Small Trees and Shrubs

description:
Whether you’ve been nervously eyeing an overgrown branch or just want to keep your trees healthy and beautiful for years to come, this practical pruning workshop with Bobby Mottern, director of horticulture at Duke Gardens, gives you the knowledge and confidence to pick up your pruners. 
You’ll start indoors with a slide presentation on pruning principles, you’ll learn: 

Why trees need pruning — and what happens when they don’t get it
When is the best time to prune for tree health
What to remove — and just as importantly, what to leave alone
How to make clean, proper cuts that help trees heal
Which tools to use, how to maintain them and how to stay safe on the job

Then head outside into the garden, where you’ll see techniques demonstrated and get the chance to try them yourself. You’ll leave with practical skills and the confidence to approach pruning in your garden. 
Fee: $28; 20% discount for Duke Gardens members with discount code. 
Location: Pelham-Cullen Classroom inside the Barnes Welcome Center. 
Accessibility: This will be a small group program that takes place partially seated indoors and partially outdoors, traveling on a combination of paved and unpaved paths with some uneven surfaces and moderate inclines. The indoor location is equipped with a hearing loop, which transmits sound directly to hearing aids and cochlear implants with a T-coil setting. Accessible restrooms are available onsite.

title: GHOST DANCE
description:
Raleigh & Triangle Activities Meetup Group
**GHOST DANCE**

**October 16, 2026** (Friday), **8**pm
Oakwood Cemetery in Downtown Raleigh
(700 Oakwood Ave.)

**ABOUT OUR GHOST DANCE**
Learn the GHOST DANCE as we dance
in the street among Night Creatures.
You'll be taught simple moves,
then we'll put the music on
and we'll be dancing in the street!
If you're not a dancer,
you can come and simply watch.

**WHERE:**
Historic Oakwood in downtown Raleigh.
Meet right outside the Oakwood Cemetery Gate
at 700 Oakwood Ave. by 8:00pm.

**PARKING:**
Park anywhere along the side streets.
There’s plenty of parking.
Note that this event takes place
OUTSIDE the cemetery.

**TIME:**
We begin at **8:00** pm.

**HOW LONG WILL IT LAST?**
This event should last about 1 hour.

**COST:** $5 (for charity)
Please have exact change (cash).
All money collected goes to help prevent cruelty to animals.

**WEBSITE:**
*[https](https://www.redsunacademy.com/ghost-walk/photos-ghost.html)[:](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S6-W4j9NmpI&feature=youtu.be)//[www.redsunacademy.com/ghost-walk](http://www.redsunacademy.com/ghost-walk/photos-ghost.html)*

**WHAT IF IT RAINS?**
This event is canceled if it rains in Raleigh that night.

**WARNING**: There will be strobe lights.
Warning given to those who are sensitive to strobe lights.
\~\~\~\~\~\~\~\~\~\~\~
**FAQ:**

**IS THIS A CHILD-FRIENDLY EVENT?**
This is mostly an event for adults and teens, tho kids can join in. However, the steps will be too challenging for small children.

**IS PARKING A PROBLEM?**
There’s plenty of parking, tho you may have to walk a block or two. Park anywhere on the surrounding neighborhood streets.

**HOW IS THIS EVENT DIFFERENT FROM PAST YEARS?**
In past years, we’ve had storytellers telling haunted tales and over a dozen 'Night Creatures' who performed scary acts as we walked the streets. Everyone loved the ZOMBIE DANCE at the end, with several people saying it was their favorite part of the evening. So to be different, we decided to have the entire evening be a GHOST DANCE!

**HOW WILL I FIND THE CHECK-IN DESK?**
Our sign-in desk is in front of the cemetery gate (a little to the left of the gate, as you face the gate from the street).

**DOES THIS TAKE PLACE IN THE CEMETERY?**
No. The cemetery closes at dark except when they have an event. We dance outside the gate, and have staff protecting us from cars and traffic.

**DO WE WEAR COSTUMES?**
It would be fun if you wear a costume, but it's optional. Some do, some don't.
..............

*[https](https://www.redsunacademy.com/ghost-walk/photos-ghost.html)[:](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S6-W4j9NmpI&feature=youtu.be)//[www.redsunacademy.com/ghost-walk/photos-ghost.html](http://www.redsunacademy.com/ghost-walk/photos-ghost.html)*

title: Play the Cyber Bowl
description:
It's time to play the third annual Cyber Bowl, a month-long competition to determine which North Carolina university is the most cyber savvy. 

 

All October long, students, faculty and staff can log into the Cyber Bowl website and take a short cybersecurity quiz. Each completed quiz earns a point for Carolina.

 

UNC-Chapel Hill faces off against nine other North Carolina universities with a lot to prove and two wins to defend. In the inaugural Cyber Bowl, Carolina won the championship by garnering the largest participation by percentage. Last year, Carolina fielded the most players — almost 2,000 — of any school.

 

The Cyber Bowl is sponsored by Information Technology Services and the Information Security Office as part of National Cybersecurity Awareness Month.

title: International Repair Day with Radical Repair
Beaver Dam Workday
description:
Triangle Off Road Cyclists (TORC)
The trail system at Beaver Dam is one of the older trails in the Triangle. This trail suffers constant erosion due to the hilly terrain and multiple streams in the area. The trail needs regular maintenance to help maintain drainage so it can reopen quickly after rain events.

**Directions: Meet at the dirt parking lot just off Creedmoor Rd, 0.5 mile before Beaver Dam park entrance.**

* Meet time: 8:45-11:00, we will distribute tools and talk about specific work to be done. We will stop earlier than 11am if it is hot.
* Duration of the workday: No more than 3 hours
* Type of Work: Moving dirt and rocks, shaping features, clearing vines and brush, de-berming, knicks and grade reversals
* Tools: Tools will be provided.
* What to bring: sturdy shoes or boots, gloves, appropriate clothing, and water

Please sign the new 2026 TORC waiver if you have not already signed. Only needs to be done once per calendar year.
[https://www.webscorer.com/register?raceid=415052](https://www.webscorer.com/register?raceid=415052)

description:
with Aimee Vandemark, Certified Forest and Nature Therapy Guide 
Forest Therapy (sometimes known as Forest Bathing or Shinrin-Yoku) broadly means taking in the forest atmosphere with all of one’s senses. Not simply a walk in the woods; it is the conscious and contemplative practice of being immersed in the sights, sounds, and smells of the forest. For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

title: America 250 at Carolina
description:
Join us for a series of events to commemorate America's 250th anniversary at the nation's first public university. The events run from Oct. 14 to 23 and include performances, poetry readings, lectures, panel discussions and more. Most of the events are free and open to the public. 

 

Visit America 250 at Carolina on the history website.

title: Play the Cyber Bowl
description:
It's time to play the third annual Cyber Bowl, a month-long competition to determine which North Carolina university is the most cyber savvy. 

 

All October long, students, faculty and staff can log into the Cyber Bowl website and take a short cybersecurity quiz. Each completed quiz earns a point for Carolina.

 

UNC-Chapel Hill faces off against nine other North Carolina universities with a lot to prove and two wins to defend. In the inaugural Cyber Bowl, Carolina won the championship by garnering the largest participation by percentage. Last year, Carolina fielded the most players — almost 2,000 — of any school.

 

The Cyber Bowl is sponsored by Information Technology Services and the Information Security Office as part of National Cybersecurity Awareness Month.

title: Mapping What Matters: A Workshop on Logic Models for Program Evaluation
description:
The Odum Institute in collaboration with Abacus Evaluation presents this 2‑hour online course that will include hands-on practice.

This course introduces participants to the use of logic models as practical tools for program evaluation.

Logic models provide a structured way to articulate program theory, clarify assumptions, and make explicit the pathways through which program inputs and activities or strategies are expected to lead to outcomes and impact. In this course, participants will learn the core components and types of logic models, examine real‑world examples, and practice developing logic models for a program or project. The course will also demonstrate how logic models can be used to guide decisions about what to measure and when.

This course is designed for anyone including researchers, program staff, and students who want a clear, systematic approach to evaluating programs and projects.

Registration and fee required to receive Zoom link access.

title: Fireside Chat with Jen Psaki
location: FedEx Global Education Center, Nelson Mandela Auditorium
description:
Join the UNC Hussman Political Communication Focus Program for a fireside chat featuring former White House press secretary Jen Psaki, moderated by Jennifer Davis, Knott Distinguished Professor of the Practice in the UNC Curriculum in Peace, War and Defense.

 

About Jen Psaki

Psaki is the anchor of MS NOW’s “The Briefing with Jen Psaki” and host of the MS NOW original podcast “The Blueprint with Jen Psaki.”

 

The former White House press secretary for President Joe Biden was lauded by the Associated Press as a communicator who “dug deep into policy, seeking an understanding that goes far beyond talking points,” and was celebrated for bringing “a mixture of warmth, humor, intelligence and edge” to her role by Vogue.

 

Prior to her time in the Biden White House, Psaki was a longtime adviser to President Barack Obama and served as a traveling press secretary on his first long-shot campaign, and later served as the White House communications director.

 

Additionally, Psaki also served as the administration’s public face on the global stage during her tenure as the State Department spokesperson, traveling the world with Secretary of State John Kerry. Psaki is also the author of “Say More: Lessons from Work, the White House, and the World” (Scribner, 2024).

 

Psaki graduated from the College of William & Mary with a double major in English and sociology. While at William & Mary, she was a member of the swim team, Chi Omega sorority and was involved in several other campus programs and activities. 

 

---

 

This event is hosted by the UNC Hussman School of Journalism and Media and is open to the Carolina community. UNC students seeking CLE credit can register on Heel Life. Pre-registration is not required for other attendees.

title: Weekly Game Night!
description:
Durham Geeks
We meet at Moon Dog Meadery under Joe Van Gogh on Broad Street every Monday night. We have loads of games (some belong to MoonDog, some are brought by attendees), a fun and welcoming group of folks (always eager to have more, however!), and there are always folks eager to teach games to those who haven't played certain titles.

Moondog has a growing collection of canned and bottled brews, ciders, and colas in addition to their in-house-brewed meads. There are also some snacks like chips and popcorn. Sometimes, folks bring in other treats to share. If you do, please mark them as containing any common allergens.

Outside food (delivered, brought in, or homemade) is welcomed and encouraged. Outside drinks are not. Since the venue does not prepare food, **dogs are allowed and welcomed.** (Dogs are very friendly and welcoming, too, but they mostly roam around to collect ear scritches and love. If you're not comfortable with dogs around, let us know, and we'll try to accommodate.)

Bring games, friends, and a welcoming spirit. We're excited to have you with us!

title: After 9/11: US National Security and Foreign Policy
location: Howell Hall , 115
description:
Twenty-five years ago, the September 11, 2001, attacks in New York and Washington, D.C. shocked the world. Dramatic changes in American life and foreign policy ensued, including new domestic security measures and the launching of the War on Terror.

Our expert panel will explain how the attacks transformed the United States and the world. Peter Feaver is a political scientist who served in George W. Bush’s White House. Landreth Freeman worked for the CIA for 22 years, specializing in counterintelligence. Chris Kojm spent decades working in US foreign policy and national security and served as deputy director of the 9/11 Commission. Joseph Stieb is a historian of U.S. military and foreign policy. Historian Michael Morgan will moderate the discussion.

Students who attend in person can earn CLE credit. No tickets necessary; seating is first-come, first-served. Reserved tickets are available for guests coming from outside Chapel Hill; email publicdiscourse@unc.edu to reserve seats. We will serve pizza after the event.

description:
Generative AI is becoming part of many everyday research workflows, from exploring a topic and evaluating information to organizing data and developing reports. In this hands-on workshop, staff from the Library AI Studio will introduce practical ways to use generative AI to support research-related tasks.

Participants will explore how to:

Use generative AI to begin researching a topic and refine questionsEvaluate AI tools and choose appropriate models for different tasksIdentify misinformation, inaccuracies, and other limitations of AI-generated contentOrganize, analyze, and manipulate data with AI-supported toolsUse AI to assist with report development and communicationMake informed decisions about when and how to incorporate AI into a research workflowThis workshop focuses on accessible, practical applications rather than advanced or specialized research computing. No prior experience with generative AI is required. Participants will have opportunities to try tools and apply strategies to their own research or information-related projects.

title: On the Rocks: A Scree & Crevice Garden Tour
location: Duke Gardens–Barnes Welcome Center, 420 Anderson Street, Durham, NC, 27705, United States
description:
At first glance, a pile of rocks seems like the last place a plant would want to call home—yet the scree and crevice gardens at Duke Gardens are bursting with an array of tenacious, beautiful and cleverly adapted plants. Join Branden Kowalyszyn, horticulturist of the Gateway Gardens at Duke Gardens, for a guided tour through these rugged landscapes, where sharp drainage, shifting gravel and thin soils support an extraordinary community of plants from around the world. Explore the artistry and science that goes into creating these gardens, including how the angle of a tilted stone, the chemistry of the gravel and the geometry of a crevice allow these plants to live here. Learn how a plant’s form, texture and growth habit reveal its survival strategies. Whether you’re a seasoned gardener looking for new ideas or someone who has walked past a rock garden and wondered what’s going on, you’ll get an insider’s look at the horticultural craft required to create these habitats and leave with an appreciation for plants’ ability to thrive even in the hardest of places. 
Fee: $24; free for Duke Gardens members with discount code. 
Parking: Parking fees apply. 
Location: Meet at the Barnes Welcome Center. 
Accessibility: This will be a small group program that takes place outdoors, traveling on a combination of paved and unpaved paths with some uneven surfaces and moderate inclines.

Judgment is the scarce skill, you guard the one-way doors, and you learn it with Claude as a tutor.
