title: John and June Allcott Gallery: taylor barnes, Weight of Light
location: Hanes Art Center, John and June Allcott Gallery
description:
Reception and gallery talk: October 29, 2026, 5:00 pm

 

Weight of Light explores how powerful emotions can be expressed through simplicity. Using bold contrasts between light and dark, the artist creates striking images that convey feeling through form, space, and gesture rather than detailed storytelling. The exhibition invites viewers to slow down and experience mood, tension, and vulnerability in a direct and deeply human way.

 

Weight of Light brings together seven works created by artist taylor barnes during her year-long residency at West Orchid in Pine Lake, Georgia. The work marks a period of experimentation and personal reflection. Drawing from her background in fibers and ceramics, barnes approaches the canvas as a site of material exploration. Through processes of staining, layering, and transforming solids into liquids and back again, she creates environments that make space for chance, absence, and emergence. The seven works resist Western linear narratives, instead functioning as maps of origin within an ongoing movement from uncertainty towards revelation. Moving between darkness and light, the works consider perception, ambiguity, and the experience of reclaiming. Existing somewhere between painting and object, these works function as thresholds. As open-ended structures, Weight of Light positions ascension as a practice of self-possession and power.

 

taylor barnes is a ceramicist and fiber artist exploring spirituality, oral history, and power through material and form. Heavily influenced by bell hooks' object/subject theories, she works with clay, fabric, string, and charcoal to translate emotion and experience into tangible presence. Black being her only color choice and philosophy, she creates work that appears restrained yet carries deep labor, lineage, ritual, and quiet intensity. barnes received her MFA in Fibers from the University of North Texas. She lives and works between Georgia and Austin, Texas.

 

Admission: Free

Gallery Hours: Monday-Friday, 8 am-5 pm

 

A weeknight or daytime permit is now required after 5:00 pm on weekdays. No permit is required from 5:00 pm Friday through 7:30 am Monday. A $1.00 one-night pass is available in selected lots. More information can be found HERE.

 

Artist website: https://www.barnesartistry.com/ 

 

For more information, please contact: Annette Lawrence, annettel@unc.edu 

 

Image credit: Courtesy of the artist

title: NC State LIVE Well-Being Concerts With Nnenna and Pierce Freelon
location: Gregg Museum of Art & Design, Galleries and Main Lobby
description:
NC State LIVE and the Gregg Museum of Art & Design have partnered to present Well-Being Concerts, featuring a family with rich connections to the university and the museum. The late architect Phil Freelon, an NC State College of Design alumnus, led the team that designed the Gregg’s new home, which opened in 2017. Phil Freelon's widow and son, Nnenna and Pierce Freelon, are a Grammy-nominated mother-son musical duo known for their collaborative children’s album, AnceStars. Nnenna Freelon is an acclaimed composer, podcaster, author and advocate for arts education. In addition to his music career, Pierce Freelon is a picture book author, podcaster and ice cream maker. The duo will perform at the Gregg inside the gallery featuring the exhibition Grounded by artist-in-residence Maya Freelon, Phil and Nnenna Freelon’s daughter. Shaped by Maya Freelon’s personal and collective memory, ancestry and humanity, Grounded transforms the Gregg into a retrospective on well-being, connection and discovery. 

This concert was created in partnership with Carnegie Hall’s Weill Music Institute. Carnegie Hall’s Well-Being Concerts combine world-class musical performances with elements of self-care and mindfulness, animated by evidence that music helps people heal and thrive.

Note: Tickets for NC State's Well-Being Concerts will go on sale on Thursday, Nov. 5, at 10 a.m. online and 1 p.m. in the box office at Thompson Hall.
source: NC State Gregg Museum of Art & Design

Holiday traditions have a way of bringing people together. The best ones feel familiar and fresh at the same time.

 

Dorrance Dance‘s The Nutcracker Suite is set to Duke Ellington and Billy Strayhorn’s extraordinary 1960 reinterpretation of the Tchaikovsky score. Part seasonal concert, part tap ballet, the production transforms the Sugar Plum Fairy into a slinky Sugar Rum Cherry, turns the “March of the Toy Soldiers” into a swinging brass “Peanut Brittle Brigade,” and gives the original ballet’s pageant of national dances a fresh 21st-century twist. 

 

Drawing on the rich traditions of tap dance to tell the story of one of the most beloved works in the holiday canon, The Nutcracker Suite is filled with rhythm, virtuosity, humor, and heart. The result is a performance that celebrates the joy of tradition while reminding us that the stories we return to year after year still evolve.

 

Student tickets always $11. Eligible for CLE. Find out more and buy tickets at: https://carolinaperformingarts.org/events/thenutcrackersuite/

The duo will perform at the Gregg inside the gallery featuring the exhibition Grounded by artist-in-residence Maya Freelon, Phil and Nnenna Freelon’s daughter. Shaped by Maya Freelon’s personal and collective memory, ancestry and humanity, Grounded transforms the Gregg into a retrospective on well-being, connection and discovery. 

This concert was created in partnership with Carnegie Hall’s Weill Music Institute. Carnegie Hall’s Well-Being Concerts combine world-class musical performances with elements of self-care and mindfulness, animated by evidence that music helps people heal and thrive.

title: John and June Allcott Gallery: taylor barnes, Weight of Light
location: Hanes Art Center, John and June Allcott Gallery
description:
Reception and gallery talk: October 29, 2026, 5:00 pm

 

Weight of Light explores how powerful emotions can be expressed through simplicity. Using bold contrasts between light and dark, the artist creates striking images that convey feeling through form, space, and gesture rather than detailed storytelling. The exhibition invites viewers to slow down and experience mood, tension, and vulnerability in a direct and deeply human way.

 

Weight of Light brings together seven works created by artist taylor barnes during her year-long residency at West Orchid in Pine Lake, Georgia. The work marks a period of experimentation and personal reflection. Drawing from her background in fibers and ceramics, barnes approaches the canvas as a site of material exploration. Through processes of staining, layering, and transforming solids into liquids and back again, she creates environments that make space for chance, absence, and emergence. The seven works resist Western linear narratives, instead functioning as maps of origin within an ongoing movement from uncertainty towards revelation. Moving between darkness and light, the works consider perception, ambiguity, and the experience of reclaiming. Existing somewhere between painting and object, these works function as thresholds. As open-ended structures, Weight of Light positions ascension as a practice of self-possession and power.

 

taylor barnes is a ceramicist and fiber artist exploring spirituality, oral history, and power through material and form. Heavily influenced by bell hooks' object/subject theories, she works with clay, fabric, string, and charcoal to translate emotion and experience into tangible presence. Black being her only color choice and philosophy, she creates work that appears restrained yet carries deep labor, lineage, ritual, and quiet intensity. barnes received her MFA in Fibers from the University of North Texas. She lives and works between Georgia and Austin, Texas.

 

Admission: Free

Gallery Hours: Monday-Friday, 8 am-5 pm

 

A weeknight or daytime permit is now required after 5:00 pm on weekdays. No permit is required from 5:00 pm Friday through 7:30 am Monday. A $1.00 one-night pass is available in selected lots. More information can be found HERE.

title: Durham Social Hack Night
description:
Triangle Developers
Hey tech folks, come out and hang at Hi-Wire starting at 6pm! Hack Night is meant to be a social evening for folks in tech. It's less about networking and more about community.

**Look for the Hack Night tabletop sign** and nerds wearing name tags to find us. If the weather is nice, we'll probably be outside.

Help folks feel welcome by using the **"Pac Man Rule"** \- when standing with a group of people \(usually in a circle\)\, leave some space open so that another person can easily join\.

See our [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/TriangleDevsSlack/policies/blob/master/code-of-conduct.md). To summarize: be nice or leave. No tolerance for harassment or oppression. In addition, since alcohol is present at these events, please be mindful of your consumption and respect other people's choices on whether or not to consume.

**FAQs**
*Do folks hack at Hack Night? Should I bring my computer?*
This is more of a night for hackers than an actual hack night. You're welcome to bring a laptop, but most people will only be socializing.

*What are the beverage options? Are there any non-alcoholic drinks?*
Hi-Wire Brewing offers many types of beers including a few non-alcoholic options plus wine and some liquor. They usually have a happy hour special on the first few beers on the menu. In the same complex are Cugino Forno which has additional drink options, and Two Roosters which has excellent ice cream.

*Are there any drink specials?*
If Hack Night is on a Tuesday, Hi-Wire usually has $5 pints for their flagship beers. Look for the list at the counter.

*Do people eat snacks/dinner during the meetup?*
Sometimes folks will order a pizza or salad from Cugino Forno. I sometimes grab an ice cream from Two Roosters across the way. Most people eat before or after but it's no big deal - whatever you prefer and are most comfortable with.

*How can I connect with the developer community?*
Go to [triangledevelopers.com](https://triangledevelopers.com/) to find the Discord and Slack info.

Thank you for signing up! Here are some notes before the phone bank.

Join Common Cause for an important phone bank as we mobilize voters to take action against dangerous legislation in state houses around the country. We will focus on the most urgent campaigns that need our help. Some of these campaigns may include stopping bills that will make it harder for millions of Americans—especially students, seniors, and veterans—to cast their ballots. We need your help to ensure voters across the country call their state representatives and demand they protect the freedom to vote.

No prior experience is necessary—our team will provide full training at the start of each shift!

## What to Expect:

* A step-by-step walkthrough of our Phone Dialer tools.

title: John and June Allcott Gallery: taylor barnes, Weight of Light
location: Hanes Art Center, John and June Allcott Gallery
description:
Reception and gallery talk: October 29, 2026, 5:00 pm

 

Weight of Light explores how powerful emotions can be expressed through simplicity. Using bold contrasts between light and dark, the artist creates striking images that convey feeling through form, space, and gesture rather than detailed storytelling. The exhibition invites viewers to slow down and experience mood, tension, and vulnerability in a direct and deeply human way.

 

Weight of Light brings together seven works created by artist taylor barnes during her year-long residency at West Orchid in Pine Lake, Georgia. The work marks a period of experimentation and personal reflection. Drawing from her background in fibers and ceramics, barnes approaches the canvas as a site of material exploration. Through processes of staining, layering, and transforming solids into liquids and back again, she creates environments that make space for chance, absence, and emergence. The seven works resist Western linear narratives, instead functioning as maps of origin within an ongoing movement from uncertainty towards revelation. Moving between darkness and light, the works consider perception, ambiguity, and the experience of reclaiming. Existing somewhere between painting and object, these works function as thresholds. As open-ended structures, Weight of Light positions ascension as a practice of self-possession and power.

 

taylor barnes is a ceramicist and fiber artist exploring spirituality, oral history, and power through material and form. Heavily influenced by bell hooks' object/subject theories, she works with clay, fabric, string, and charcoal to translate emotion and experience into tangible presence. Black being her only color choice and philosophy, she creates work that appears restrained yet carries deep labor, lineage, ritual, and quiet intensity. barnes received her MFA in Fibers from the University of North Texas. She lives and works between Georgia and Austin, Texas.

 

Admission: Free

Gallery Hours: Monday-Friday, 8 am-5 pm

 

A weeknight or daytime permit is now required after 5:00 pm on weekdays. No permit is required from 5:00 pm Friday through 7:30 am Monday. A $1.00 one-night pass is available in selected lots. More information can be found HERE.

Please join our virtual welcome session with this link

Are you a young person between 13 and 25 years old who is interested in taking action around preventing gun violence? Join us for our Team ENOUGH welcome session to learn more about the different ways you can engage. 

Team ENOUGH is a youth-led program whose mission is to educate young voices about gun violence and mobilize them to take meaningful action against it. Supported by Brady United, we harness the expertise and experience of today’s youth to advance our intersectional work across the country. 

Led by an Executive Council, comprised of students just like us, we believe that diversity is a strength, and that only when everyone has a seat at the table can we build an effective movement to prevent all gun violence in all communities.

For us, preventing gun violence not only requires regulating access to firearms but also addressing how systemic racism and environmental factors cause this form of bloodshed to run especially rampant in communities of color. You cannot talk about gun violence without talking about police brutality, white supremacy, the broken criminal justice system, poverty, homophobia, access to affordable housing, or the often barriers separating disadvantaged populations from physical and mental healthcare. 

So if you share this belief, join us for our Team ENOUGH welcome session and become part of the movement to end gun violence in our lifetime.

title: Dec 10 - AI, ML and Computer Vision Meetup
description:
Raleigh AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join our virtual meetup to hear talks from experts on cutting-edge topics across AI, ML, and computer vision.

**Date, Time and Location**

Dec 10, 2026
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/ai-ml-and-computer-vision-meetup-december-10-2026)**

**Your mAP is fine. Your slices are not. Finding the images that actually matter**

A single mAP can look acceptable while one slice is unusable, small objects, occlusion, or a confused class. I will run a pretrained detector on a few hundred public images (COCO-style, not a production crawl), report the headline metric, then break the same run by slice and walk through the worst samples.

The claim is modest: you do not need a million images or a trained-from-scratch model to see what the mean is hiding, and you cannot relabel everything, so the next labeling budget should follow those slices. No employer data and no confidential dashboards.

*About the Speaker*

[Amandeep Jiddewar](https://www.linkedin.com/in/amanfj/) is a Machine Learning Engineer at Pinterest, with prior work in U.S. manufacturing analytics (CertainTeed / Saint-Gobain) and marketplace allocation (QuinStreet). Emory Goizueta MSBA (2019), Kaggle Expert. This talk is in his personal capacity and does not represent his current or prior employers.

**Production AI Agents: Tool Use, Evaluation, Guardrails and Observability**

Building an AI agent is easy. Knowing whether it is behaving reliably in production is much harder. This session explores how to evaluate agents that use tools and external systems, including tool-call validation, tracing, observability, failure analysis, guardrails, permissions, and human review.

Attendees will learn practical patterns for understanding not just what an agent answered, but why it acted and whether the action was safe.

*About the Speaker*

[Akshay Talathi](https://www.linkedin.com/in/akshaytalathi/) is a Vice President at Goldman Sachs with over 10 years of experience building large-scale, cloud-native, and distributed systems across financial services and technology. His current focus is GenAI and agentic AI, including production AI agents, MCP, enterprise integrations, guardrails, observability, and reliable AI-driven workflows.

**From Virtual Worlds to Physical AI: Building Simulation Pipelines That Survive the Real World**

Robots are moving beyond perception systems that only detect and classify objects toward systems that must understand a scene, learn behaviors, and act in the physical world. In this talk, I’ll show a practical Physical AI workflow using OpenUSD, BowerBot, NVIDIA Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab to build a robot’s virtual world, including its body, cameras, sensors, and environment.

We’ll explore how demonstrations and reinforcement learning can teach behaviors in simulation, how vision and sensor data become observations for a robot policy, and what needs to match when transferring that behavior to real hardware. The demo follows a small robot from a simulated environment toward a real-world task, exposing both the power and the limitations of sim-to-real.

The goal is to make the path from pixels to actions concrete for computer vision and machine learning practitioners.

*About the Speaker*

[Arturo Morales Rangel](https://www.linkedin.com/in/arturo-morales-rangel) is the founder of Binary Core LLC, a Physical AI engineering company working across simulation, perception, robot learning, and deployment.

title: Carolina History Tour
description:
Learn more about the history of the nation’s first public university by attending a Carolina History Tour. The Carolina History Tours cover more than 200 years of the history of UNC-Chapel Hill, including the establishment of the university in the 18th century, the history of campus landmarks including the Old Well, Davie Poplar, and Unsung Founders Memorial, the push to open enrollment to all North Carolinians, and the growth of the school in the 20th and 21st centuries. Tours will begin at the Old Well and finish at Wilson Library. Most tours last a little over an hour. 

Led by staff from the Wilson Special Collections Library, these tours are part of the University Library’s commitment to collecting, preserving, and sharing the history of the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. 

Registration is required. You can register for your spot here.

title: Digital Accessibility Pop-Up Labs
location: Carolina Union, 2502
description:
The POP Lab is a drop-in workspace where UNC faculty and staff can make progress with support from digital accessibility consultants. Bring your documents, course materials, websites, reports, or questions, and work at your own pace. Come by for a few minutes or stay for the full session to ask questions, explore tools, solve problems and make meaningful progress toward expanding access.

 

Progress Over Perfection

Progress means recognizing common barriers in the platforms you use and taking small steps to reduce them. It’s choosing web formats over PDFs, applying table headers, checking color contrast and collaborating on accessible templates so everyone can start from a strong foundation. Digital accessibility depends on steady, intentional progress, not perfection, to expand access for all.

title: *IN-PERSON* SF/F Group
description:
Durham Writers Group
We will be at the Moon House at 3039 University Dr. in Durham. This venue does not serve food or drink, but feel free to bring your own. There is a kitchenette for our use, but be sure to clean up afterwards. The space might be a little cozy; please consider masking or staying home if you have a respiratory ailment.

This sub-group focuses on Speculative Fiction, including Science Fiction, Fantasy and Horror. If you have anything that falls under that category — be it short story, poem, novel-in-progress or screenplay — then come! We'd love to hear from you.

Our format allows each reader 15 minutes to present their work aloud, followed by approximately 20 minutes of feedback from the other attendees. To ensure fairness, each attendee is limited to 1 minute of Initial Feedback time. During that period, the author remains silent. Next, we have a 5 minute Free-For-All discussion about the work -- then the author may speak. (We usually get through three readers.)

Though not required, in order to receive more in-depth feed-back, readers may post their work in advance on our Google Group:
https://groups.google.com/d/forum/durham-sff-writers-group

We ask that participants keep their comments constructive and respectful, focusing on what works or doesn't work in the piece.

We also ask that readers provide a warning, both on the Google Group and during the meeting, if their story features content that some readers might find upsetting. This includes descriptions of violence or sexual content.

location: Virtual event
description:

How to join:
Please join our virtual welcome session with this link

Are you a young person between 13 and 25 years old who is interested in taking action around preventing gun violence? Join us for our Team ENOUGH welcome session to learn more about the different ways you can engage. 

Team ENOUGH is a youth-led program whose mission is to educate young voices about gun violence and mobilize them to take meaningful action against it. Supported by Brady United, we harness the expertise and experience of today’s youth to advance our intersectional work across the country. 

Led by an Executive Council, comprised of students just like us, we believe that diversity is a strength, and that only when everyone has a seat at the table can we build an effective movement to prevent all gun violence in all communities.

For us, preventing gun violence not only requires regulating access to firearms but also addressing how systemic racism and environmental factors cause this form of bloodshed to run especially rampant in communities of color. You cannot talk about gun violence without talking about police brutality, white supremacy, the broken criminal justice system, poverty, homophobia, access to affordable housing, or the often barriers separating disadvantaged populations from physical and mental healthcare. 

So if you share this belief, join us for our Team ENOUGH welcome session and become part of the movement to end gun violence in our lifetime.

How to prepare:
We are excited to see you soon!

P.S. This is a call for young people from 13-25 years old who are interested in getting engaged with the Team ENOUGH program. If you are over the age of 25 please sign up for the Brady Welcome Session at https://www.mobilize.us/brady/event/274016/

How to join:
Thank you for signing up! Here are some notes before the phone bank.

This phone bank will be easier if you are **not doing everything on your phone or tablet**, we recommend you use two devices, preferably a phone and a computer, and we highly recommend you join us at home or in a quiet area. 

We will be using Scale to Win to make calls. 

**Please click this link and [watch a quick training on how to use Scale to Win](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cMqsfqpHPvU).**

Join Common Cause for an important phone bank as we mobilize voters to take action against dangerous legislation in state houses around the country. We will focus on the most urgent campaigns that need our help. Some of these campaigns may include stopping bills that will make it harder for millions of Americans—especially students, seniors, and veterans—to cast their ballots. We need your help to ensure voters across the country call their state representatives and demand they protect the freedom to vote.

No prior experience is necessary—our team will provide full training at the start of each shift!

## What to Expect:

* A step-by-step walkthrough of our Phone Dialer tools.
* Expert tips on effective communication with voters.
* Opportunities to ask questions and connect with other like-minded volunteers.


Sign up today and take the first step toward empowering voters and protecting democracy in 2025!

How to join:
Thank you for signing up! Here are some notes before the phone bank.

This phone bank will be easier if you are **not doing everything on your phone or tablet**, we recommend you use two devices, preferably a phone and a computer, and we highly recommend you join us at home or in a quiet area. 

We will be using Scale to Win to make calls. 

**Please click this link and [watch a quick training on how to use Scale to Win](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cMqsfqpHPvU).**

Join Common Cause for an important phone bank as we mobilize voters to take action against dangerous legislation in state houses around the country. We will focus on the most urgent campaigns that need our help. Some of these campaigns may include stopping bills that will make it harder for millions of Americans—especially students, seniors, and veterans—to cast their ballots. We need your help to ensure voters across the country call their state representatives and demand they protect the freedom to vote.

No prior experience is necessary—our team will provide full training at the start of each shift!

## What to Expect:

* A step-by-step walkthrough of our Phone Dialer tools.
* Expert tips on effective communication with voters.
* Opportunities to ask questions and connect with other like-minded volunteers.


Sign up today and take the first step toward empowering voters and protecting democracy in 2025!

description:

How to join:
Please join our virtual welcome session with this link

Are you a young person between 13 and 25 years old who is interested in taking action around preventing gun violence? Join us for our Team ENOUGH welcome session to learn more about the different ways you can engage. 

Team ENOUGH is a youth-led program whose mission is to educate young voices about gun violence and mobilize them to take meaningful action against it. Supported by Brady United, we harness the expertise and experience of today’s youth to advance our intersectional work across the country. 

Led by an Executive Council, comprised of students just like us, we believe that diversity is a strength, and that only when everyone has a seat at the table can we build an effective movement to prevent all gun violence in all communities.

For us, preventing gun violence not only requires regulating access to firearms but also addressing how systemic racism and environmental factors cause this form of bloodshed to run especially rampant in communities of color. You cannot talk about gun violence without talking about police brutality, white supremacy, the broken criminal justice system, poverty, homophobia, access to affordable housing, or the often barriers separating disadvantaged populations from physical and mental healthcare. 

So if you share this belief, join us for our Team ENOUGH welcome session and become part of the movement to end gun violence in our lifetime.

How to prepare:
We are excited to see you soon!

P.S. This is a call for young people from 13-25 years old who are interested in getting engaged with the Team ENOUGH program. If you are over the age of 25 please sign up for the Brady Welcome Session at https://www.mobilize.us/brady/event/274016/

Thank you for signing up! Here are some notes before the phone bank.

This phone bank will be easier if you are **not doing everything on your phone or tablet**, we recommend you use two devices, preferably a phone and a computer, and we highly recommend you join us at home or in a quiet area.

We need your help to ensure voters across the country call their state representatives and demand they protect the freedom to vote.

* Opportunities to ask questions and connect with other like-minded volunteers.

How to join:
Thank you for signing up! Here are some notes before the phone bank.

This phone bank will be easier if you are **not doing everything on your phone or tablet**, we recommend you use two devices, preferably a phone and a computer, and we highly recommend you join us at home or in a quiet area. 

We will be using Scale to Win to make calls. 

**Please click this link and [watch a quick training on how to use Scale to Win](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cMqsfqpHPvU).**

Join Common Cause for an important phone bank as we mobilize voters to take action against dangerous legislation in state houses around the country. We will focus on the most urgent campaigns that need our help. Some of these campaigns may include stopping bills that will make it harder for millions of Americans—especially students, seniors, and veterans—to cast their ballots. We need your help to ensure voters across the country call their state representatives and demand they protect the freedom to vote.

No prior experience is necessary—our team will provide full training at the start of each shift!

## What to Expect:

* A step-by-step walkthrough of our Phone Dialer tools.
* Expert tips on effective communication with voters.
* Opportunities to ask questions and connect with other like-minded volunteers.


Sign up today and take the first step toward empowering voters and protecting democracy in 2025!

title: Wednesday night meditation circle
description:
Durham Plum Village Meditation Circle
Join us for a meditation circle in the Plum Village tradition of Buddhist teacher Thich Nhat Hanh. We will practice a short seated meditation (10 minutes), walking meditation (10 minutes), dharma share on a topic of mindfulness by a fellow practitioner, group dharma sharing, and singing. We actively welcome and affirm BIPOC and queer people and seek to hold an inclusive space for all.

**Please note: Our location has changed to the Durham Friends Meetinghouse building in the Dogwood Room at 404 Alexander Ave, Durham, NC 27705**

The space has accessible parking, entrances, and gender neutral bathrooms. Chairs are available, and we encourage you to bring a cushion with you if you have one.

Our group is spirited, compassionate, and eager to learn mindfulness practices in community with one another. We have a suggested $0-5 donation to cover the cost of the space, with excess donations put toward group materials like spare cushions.

Please consider donating to our group on Venmo: [@DurhamPlumVillageMeditation](https://account.venmo.com/u/durhamplumvillagemeditation)

If you would like to be on our sangha email list, please reach out to durhamplumvillagemeditation@gmail.comd

How to join:
Thank you for signing up! Here are some notes before the phone bank.

This phone bank will be easier if you are **not doing everything on your phone or tablet**, we recommend you use two devices, preferably a phone and a computer, and we highly recommend you join us at home or in a quiet area. 

We will be using Scale to Win to make calls. 

**Please click this link and [watch a quick training on how to use Scale to Win](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cMqsfqpHPvU).**

Join Common Cause for an important phone bank as we mobilize voters to take action against dangerous legislation in state houses around the country. We will focus on the most urgent campaigns that need our help. Some of these campaigns may include stopping bills that will make it harder for millions of Americans—especially students, seniors, and veterans—to cast their ballots. We need your help to ensure voters across the country call their state representatives and demand they protect the freedom to vote.

No prior experience is necessary—our team will provide full training at the start of each shift!

## What to Expect:

* A step-by-step walkthrough of our Phone Dialer tools.
* Expert tips on effective communication with voters.
* Opportunities to ask questions and connect with other like-minded volunteers.


Sign up today and take the first step toward empowering voters and protecting democracy in 2025!

title: Get Shit Done - SQSN
location: 114 - living room
description: This event is intended for Queer and/or Trans survivors:Some of the biggest barriers to survivor safety are finance related. While we do our best to put cash directly into survivors hands, in tandem, we thought it would be awesome to create a body doubling/coworking space where we can support each other in sifting through all the shit that goes into getting financial stable. And offer relevant financial resources as we find them!That’s why we host our “Get Shit Done” evenings. They will occur the 1st & 3rd Tuesday of each month and be available in person or online (must register or email advocate@lgbtqcenterofdurham.org for the virtual link). If you or someone you know is a money expert who wants to share their knowledge with queer/trans survivors, please reach out!

title: Mastermind
location: Wake Forest, NC
description: Mastermind is back! We're excited to bring back one of our favorite small business programs in partnership with Pinnacle Financial Partners. Think of Mastermind as a six-week, low-commitment accelerator for your business. A small, focused group designed to help you step out of the day-to-day and spend intentional time working ON your business. Using the E-Myth Revisited by Michael Gerver as a guide, participants will work through practical conversations around building a stronger, more productive and sustainable business. The real value comes from the room: sharing ideas, learning from other business owners, challenging your own thinking and leaving each week with something you can put to work. Mastermind is intentionally designed to be manageable. Give us one hour a week for six weeks, come ready to particpate, and put in a little work between sessions. Pinnacle will provide the structure, conversation, and accountability to help you look at your business differently.

title: “To BEethoven Rather Than To Seem”: Part III | Gut Instinct Chamber Music Project
location: Person Hall
description:
FEATURING

Nicholas DiEguenio, violin
Mimi Solomon, piano

 

PROGRAM

Featuring Beethoven’s heroic and youthful Violin Sonata No. 3 and the Jesse Jones Scherzo it inspired

This season, Gut Instinct takes on the large-scale project “To Beethoven Rather Than To Seem,” marking 200 years since Beethoven’s death and 250 since the U.S. Declaration of Independence. Over the course of five concerts, Nicholas DiEugenio and pianist Mimi Solomon will present all ten Beethoven Sonatas on period instruments along with five commissioned works written expressly for them.

 

PARKING

Please plan to arrive early as parking on campus can be tricky. Learn more about parking and directions to UNC-Chapel Hill’s campus.

 

The Gut Instinct Chamber Music Project, now in its third season, is a concert series in the Triangle area which brings UNC-Chapel Hill and Duke University’s historical instrument collections together with artists committed to presenting inspired, visceral, historically informed performances of the 19th-century chamber music repertoire. The series features music of female composers and their artistic circles. The name “Gut Instinct” is a play on words. In 19th-century Europe, the violin, viola, and cello were strung with (sheep) gut.

 

All of the artists collaborating with the Pleyel and Graf pianos at UNC-Chapel Hill (built in 19th-century Paris and Vienna, respectively), as well as the Clementi piano at Duke (early 19th-century England) use these gut string materials. The turn of phrase “gut instinct” also refers to the visceral, accessible nature of the musical performances that this series presents. Our mission is to make “Historically Informed Performance” accessible, relatable, and culturally relevant! We also want to feature these special pianos that are rarely heard by the public, along with great music by female composers which has remained lesser known to the greater public for far too long, and living composers who are keeping our art form alive!

title: Durham Social Hack Night
description:
Triangle Developers
Hey tech folks, come out and hang at Hi-Wire starting at 6pm! Hack Night is meant to be a social evening for folks in tech. It's less about networking and more about community.

**Look for the Hack Night tabletop sign** and nerds wearing name tags to find us. If the weather is nice, we'll probably be outside.

Help folks feel welcome by using the **"Pac Man Rule"** \- when standing with a group of people \(usually in a circle\)\, leave some space open so that another person can easily join\.

See our [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/TriangleDevsSlack/policies/blob/master/code-of-conduct.md). To summarize: be nice or leave. No tolerance for harassment or oppression. In addition, since alcohol is present at these events, please be mindful of your consumption and respect other people's choices on whether or not to consume.

**FAQs**
*Do folks hack at Hack Night? Should I bring my computer?*
This is more of a night for hackers than an actual hack night. You're welcome to bring a laptop, but most people will only be socializing.

*What are the beverage options? Are there any non-alcoholic drinks?*
Hi-Wire Brewing offers many types of beers including a few non-alcoholic options plus wine and some liquor. They usually have a happy hour special on the first few beers on the menu. In the same complex are Cugino Forno which has additional drink options, and Two Roosters which has excellent ice cream.

*Are there any drink specials?*
If Hack Night is on a Tuesday, Hi-Wire usually has $5 pints for their flagship beers. Look for the list at the counter.

*Do people eat snacks/dinner during the meetup?*
Sometimes folks will order a pizza or salad from Cugino Forno. I sometimes grab an ice cream from Two Roosters across the way. Most people eat before or after but it's no big deal - whatever you prefer and are most comfortable with.

*How can I connect with the developer community?*
Go to [triangledevelopers.com](https://triangledevelopers.com/) to find the Discord and Slack info.

title: Monthly Welcome, Community, and Project Meeting
description:
Code with the Carolinas - Triangle
Code with the Carolinas is a community of people working together as civic tech volunteers to improve wellbeing in North and South Carolina, and we invite you to join us for our biweekly online meetings!
Our meetings start with introductions, updates on old and new business, and status reports on current projects, emphasizing how you can get involved. All are welcome and no technical skills are needed.

**Typical Agenda**
Introductions
Organizational Updates
Project updates

* Active projects like Zoning Atlas
* Proposal development for new projects

Meetings are on the Jitsi platform and the link is provided before each meeting. If you will be joining on mobile, install the Jitsi app in advance [https://jitsi.org/downloads/](https://jitsi.org/downloads/) If you joined on mobile and your audio isn't working, it might be because you joined through a browser and not through the app.

Learn more at [[codewiththecarolinas.org](http://codewiththecarolinas.org/)]([http://codeforthecarolinas.org](http://codeforthecarolinas.org/)), [join our Slack](https://join.slack.com/t/codewiththecarolinas/shared_invite/zt-3i6ptx0pz-raH_7Zx4sX0wFUkYM9w3Zw), or reach out to [info@codewiththecarolinas.org](http://info@codewiththecarolinas.org/)

title: earspace | CMM 26-27
location: Hill Hall, Moeser Auditorium
description:
FEATURING

earspace

earspace is an ensemble consisting of violin, viola, cello, flute, oboe, clarinet, piano, and percussion that performs a combination of conducted and unconducted chamber music of a wide variety of scopes. Passionate producers, the ensemble is dedicated to both commissioning new, immersive works and amplifying rarely-performed gems of the repertoire. Founded in North Carolina, the group is now based across the US and performs regularly around the east coast, collaborating with organizations including the Southern Exposure New Music Series, Towson University, Duke University, UNC Chapel Hill, the Peabody Institute, Asheville Ballet, Carolina Performing Arts, and others.

The ensemble seeks to expose the inherent potentials within every moment and space, cultivating visceral reactions unique to every manifestation. Through their projects, they explore the extremities of contemporary performance and work to bring audiences closer to the music they experience.

title: Dr. Maria Ryan | UNC Music Research Forum
location: Person Hall
description:
Dr. Maria Ryan, Florida State University

“Title TBA”



 

Assistant Professor of Musicology Maria Ryan researches and writes about how African and African-descended people in the Americas theorized, performed, and listened to music with European origins in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. Ryan’s in-process book project, Ambivalent Listening: Race, Music, and Slavery in the British Colonial Caribbean 1750–1838, investigates the relationship between race and music in the British colonial Caribbean, exploring the many ways that African-descended musicians and listeners engaged with music with European origins. This work is supported in 2024–25 by an ACLS Fellowship, NEH Fellowship, and Citizens and Scholars Career Enhancement Fellowship. Early work from this project can be seen in the Journal of the Society for American Music and Journal of the American Musicological Society. In addition to her work on music in the British colonial Caribbean, Ryan researches and teaches Black feminist theory, the intellectual history of Black music, and book history and archive studies. Ryan is a Senior Fellow in Critical Bibliography at the Rare Book School, where she focuses on methods for recuperating Black listening practices from sources created under colonial logics. Ryan’s work has been supported by grants and fellowships from ACLS/Mellon, American Musicological Society, American Historical Association, Society for American Music, and Library Company of Philadelphia. She holds the B.A. degree from the University of Nottingham, the M.Mus. degree from King’s College London, and the Ph.D. in musicology with a certificate in Africana studies from the University of Pennsylvania.

 

The UNC Music Research Forum hosts invited lectures by distinguished music scholars from around the world and informal research presentations by members of our department and colleagues across campus. It serves as an intellectual hub for the department and is open to all. The Forum is usually held on the final Friday of each month during the semester from 3:30-5:00 pm in Person Recital Hall.

title: Cognitive Interviewing in Survey Research
description:
Cognitive interviewing in survey research is a tool that allows researchers to improve survey questions and questionnaires by better understanding how respondents understand and respond to the questions they are being asked. Data gathered through cognitive interviews help researchers identify and remedy issues with their questionnaires. This short course provides participants with fundamentals on where cognitive interviews fit in the survey process and on how to design, conduct, and analyze cognitive interviews. Participants will have the opportunity to practice specific cognitive interviewing techniques, including think-alouds, probing, and observation. Participants will also learn about revising survey questions based on interpreting cognitive interview results and about the research on which cognitive interview practices are based.

Course Goals:
By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
1. Understand what cognitive interviews are and their use in survey research
2. Be able to prepare for and conduct cognitive interviews
3. Improve survey questionnaires and survey items based on cognitive interview data

 

Registration and fee (refundable for Carolina students) are required for Zoom link access.

This event is sponsored by the UNC Odum Institute.

title: Durham Social Hack Night
description:
Triangle Developers
Hey tech folks, come out and hang at Hi-Wire starting at 6pm! Hack Night is meant to be a social evening for folks in tech. It's less about networking and more about community.

**Look for the Hack Night tabletop sign** and nerds wearing name tags to find us. If the weather is nice, we'll probably be outside.

Help folks feel welcome by using the **"Pac Man Rule"** \- when standing with a group of people \(usually in a circle\)\, leave some space open so that another person can easily join\.

See our [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/TriangleDevsSlack/policies/blob/master/code-of-conduct.md). To summarize: be nice or leave. No tolerance for harassment or oppression. In addition, since alcohol is present at these events, please be mindful of your consumption and respect other people's choices on whether or not to consume.

**FAQs**
*Do folks hack at Hack Night? Should I bring my computer?*
This is more of a night for hackers than an actual hack night. You're welcome to bring a laptop, but most people will only be socializing.

*What are the beverage options? Are there any non-alcoholic drinks?*
Hi-Wire Brewing offers many types of beers including a few non-alcoholic options plus wine and some liquor. They usually have a happy hour special on the first few beers on the menu. In the same complex are Cugino Forno which has additional drink options, and Two Roosters which has excellent ice cream.

*Are there any drink specials?*
If Hack Night is on a Tuesday, Hi-Wire usually has $5 pints for their flagship beers. Look for the list at the counter.

*Do people eat snacks/dinner during the meetup?*
Sometimes folks will order a pizza or salad from Cugino Forno. I sometimes grab an ice cream from Two Roosters across the way. Most people eat before or after but it's no big deal - whatever you prefer and are most comfortable with.

*How can I connect with the developer community?*
Go to [triangledevelopers.com](https://triangledevelopers.com/) to find the Discord and Slack info.

description:
The African American Cultural Center and our campus partners invite the university community and the public to our annual Symposium on Afrofuturism and Diasporic Scholarship. Our focus this year connects to our 55th anniversary and the theme of Legacy, Libations and Liberation. 

The symposium will feature African diasporic learning, scholarship and epistemologies via cutting-edge research, storytelling, creative works, discussion circles, community-based projects and industry initiatives from the NC State and the surrounding community. The symposium will include oral presentations, roundtables, poster presentations, creative practices, keynote speakers, panels and networking opportunities. 

We welcome submissions to present at the conference from students, staff, faculty, alumni, community members and surrounding university and college partners. For a full description of the symposium, including information on submitting a proposal, visit our website.
source: NC State African American Cultural Center

title: Social Media as Qualitative Data: A Design Framework
description:
Conversations that take place online – from learning management systems to Signal chats to Discord groups to Reddit support groups and Instagram influencing – can be valuable forms of evidence for qualitative researchers. In this workshop, participants will create their own research designs to investigate a phenomenon of interest, as evidenced through social media data, in a systematic and rigorous way. The Paulus and Wise research design decision framework will scaffold learners in how to identify an object of interest; articulate their philosophical and theoretical assumptions about how language functions online; create focused and relevant research questions; ensure methodological alignment across aspects of the study design; resolve ethical dilemmas around treating social media as data; extract and transform social media into a coherent dataset; select appropriate technologies for managing and analyzing data; perform a systematic narrative, discourse and/or thematic analysis; and establish the quality of the findings. Course material will be drawn from “Looking for Learning, Insight and Transformation in Online Talk” (Paulus & Wise, Routledge, 2019).

Registration and fee are required for Zoom link access. Space is limited! Please visit course website for more information and registration.

title: “To BEethoven Rather Than To Seem”: Part IV | Gut Instinct Chamber Music Project
location: Person Hall
description:
FEATURING

Nicholas DiEguenio, violin
Mimi Solomon, piano

 

PROGRAM

Featuring Beethoven’s final Violin Sonata, the elegiac and enigmatic op. 96, along with Tonia Ko’s Tribute: Axis II

This season, Gut Instinct takes on the large-scale project “To Beethoven Rather Than To Seem,” marking 200 years since Beethoven’s death and 250 since the U.S. Declaration of Independence. Over the course of five concerts, Nicholas DiEugenio and pianist Mimi Solomon will present all ten Beethoven Sonatas on period instruments along with five commissioned works written expressly for them.

This concert is presented as part of the NCHIP Festival.

 

ADMISSION

Free, no reservation required.

 

PARKING

Please plan to arrive early as parking on campus can be tricky. Learn more about parking and directions to UNC-Chapel Hill’s campus.

 

The Gut Instinct Chamber Music Project, now in its third season, is a concert series in the Triangle area which brings UNC-Chapel Hill and Duke University’s historical instrument collections together with artists committed to presenting inspired, visceral, historically informed performances of the 19th-century chamber music repertoire. The series features music of female composers and their artistic circles. The name “Gut Instinct” is a play on words. In 19th-century Europe, the violin, viola, and cello were strung with (sheep) gut.

 

All of the artists collaborating with the Pleyel and Graf pianos at UNC-Chapel Hill (built in 19th-century Paris and Vienna, respectively), as well as the Clementi piano at Duke (early 19th-century England) use these gut string materials. The turn of phrase “gut instinct” also refers to the visceral, accessible nature of the musical performances that this series presents. Our mission is to make “Historically Informed Performance” accessible, relatable, and culturally relevant! We also want to feature these special pianos that are rarely heard by the public, along with great music by female composers which has remained lesser known to the greater public for far too long, and living composers who are keeping our art form alive!

title: Learning Lab: Fashion Sustainability and Makerspace
location: D.H. Hill Jr. Library, Makerspace
description:
Don’t throw it away, rework it.

Join the African American Cultural Center at the D.H. Hill Jr. Library Makerspace for a hands-on dive into sustainable fashion and do-it-yourself creation. Whether you want to learn the basics of how to use a sewing machine, mend your favorite damaged thrifted piece or embroider custom patches to personalize your jacket or tote, this lab is for you. We’ll cover essential mending techniques and show you how to extend the life of your wardrobe through conscious creation. Sewing experience is not necessary to participate.

We'll provide all machines and materials needed for the session. Bring a piece of clothing you’d like to mend or customize or use the practice fabric provided

If you have questions about the session, contact Andaiye Qaasim, assistant director of the African American Cultural Center, at aaqaasim@ncsu.edu.
source: NC State African American Cultural Center

title: The Surge: An Ode to Sinéad O’Connor
location: Memorial Hall
description:
For anyone who has ever questioned their place, pushed against expectations, or wondered what it costs to remain true to yourself, The Surge: An Ode to Sinéad O’Connor is for you.

Inspired by the music, words, and enduring spirit of Sinéad O’Connor, director and choreographer Sonya Tayeh creates a powerful dance experience performed by ten women over the age of 40. O’Connor’s music and narration, drawn from her memoir Rememberings, weave throughout the performance. 

 

The Surge is a reflection on identity, aging, freedom, and the courage required to live authentically in a world that often rewards conformity. What emerges is both deeply personal and unexpectedly communal: a celebration of women who refuse to disappear, soften themselves for others, or surrender the right to define their own lives.

 

Student tickets always $11. Eligible for CLE. Find out more and buy tickets at: https://carolinaperformingarts.org/events/the-surge/

location: Person Hall, Recital Hall
description:
Dr. Eric Debrah-Otchere, University of Cape Coast, National Humanities Center

“Title TBA”

 

Eric Debrah Otchere teaches in the Department of Music and Dance (Faculty of Arts, College of Humanities and Legal Studies) at the University of Cape Coast, Ghana. He specializes in the field(s) of Music Education/Music Psychology and handles various courses at both the undergraduate and graduate levels. He is the recipient of several prestigious awards/fellowships such as a Presidential Fellow of the African Studies Association (USA), AHP-ACLS/Rhodes University Post-Doctoral Fellow, and a Stellenbosch Institute for Advanced Studies (STIAS) Iso Lomso Fellow. His research interests cover areas in Music Education (e.g. pedagogy, philosophy, curriculum, research methods) and Music Psychology (e.g. music and emotions, musical development, music preferences, music cognition, emotional intelligence, health and wellbeing). He has a number of publications in International peer-reviewed journals, some of which he has also reviewed papers for.

 

The UNC Music Research Forum hosts invited lectures by distinguished music scholars from around the world and informal research presentations by members of our department and colleagues across campus. It serves as an intellectual hub for the department and is open to all. The Forum is usually held on the final Friday of each month during the semester from 3:30-5:00 pm in Person Recital Hall.

 

Admission: Free, No Reservation Required

title: The Vijay Iyer Quartet
location: Memorial Hall
description:
Some performances—especially jazz—invite you to surrender the need to know what’s coming next. You stop trying to predict the next note and simply hold your breath, waiting to discover where the music will lead. That uncertainty is the thrill: performers and audience alike following the sound somewhere unexpected, until you find yourself wondering, How did they do that?

 

The Vijay Iyer Quartet lives in that space of possibility. Performing compositions by composer-pianist Vijay Iyer, the ensemble reveals new possibilities in the music each time it takes the stage.

 

Voted DownBeat‘s Jazz Artist of the Year four times and a MacArthur Fellow, Iyer has spent decades expanding the possibilities of the jazz quartet. His celebrated trio with bassist Linda May Han Oh and drummer Tyshawn Sorey was praised by The New York Times as “one of the best bands in jazz.”

 

Building on three decades of musical collaboration and experimentation, Iyer expanded the ensemble in 2025 with the addition of trumpeter Adam O’Farrill, a longtime collaborator and member of one of Afro-Latin music’s most revered musical families.

 

Together, the quartet combines acoustic instruments with Fender Rhodes and electronics, creating music that is fearless, unpredictable, and constantly unfolding.

title: Che Apalache
location: Hill Hall, Moeser Auditorium
description:
What do you get when you blend Appalachian bluegrass and old-time music with Latin American folk traditions including flamenco, murga, and candombe? You get Che Apalache’s acclaimed Latingrass! 

 

Founder Joe Troop grew up in North Carolina and taught music in Buenos Aires after graduating from UNC. His students became his bandmates: Pau Barjau on banjo, Franco Martino on guitar, and Omar Ruiz-Lopez on mandolin.

 

Rooted in traditions that span continents, the band grew out of a willingness to follow interests across languages, cultures, and traditions. What emerged is a sound shaped by relationships, shared experiences, and a genuine openness to learning from one another.

title: NC State LIVE Well-Being Concerts With Nnenna and Pierce Freelon
location: Gregg Museum of Art & Design, Galleries and Main Lobby
description:
NC State LIVE and the Gregg Museum of Art & Design have partnered to present Well-Being Concerts, featuring a family with rich connections to the university and the museum. The late architect Phil Freelon, an NC State College of Design alumnus, led the team that designed the Gregg’s new home, which opened in 2017. Phil Freelon's widow and son, Nnenna and Pierce Freelon, are a Grammy-nominated mother-son musical duo known for their collaborative children’s album, AnceStars. Nnenna Freelon is an acclaimed composer, podcaster, author and advocate for arts education. In addition to his music career, Pierce Freelon is a picture book author, podcaster and ice cream maker. The duo will perform at the Gregg inside the gallery featuring the exhibition Grounded by artist-in-residence Maya Freelon, Phil and Nnenna Freelon’s daughter. Shaped by Maya Freelon’s personal and collective memory, ancestry and humanity, Grounded transforms the Gregg into a retrospective on well-being, connection and discovery. 

This concert was created in partnership with Carnegie Hall’s Weill Music Institute. Carnegie Hall’s Well-Being Concerts combine world-class musical performances with elements of self-care and mindfulness, animated by evidence that music helps people heal and thrive.

Note: Tickets for NC State's Well-Being Concerts will go on sale on Thursday, Nov. 5, at 10 a.m. online and 1 p.m. in the box office at Thompson Hall.
source: NC State Gregg Museum of Art & Design

title: Emanuel Ax, piano & Yo-Yo Ma, cello
location: Memorial Hall
description:
To be in the room when Yo-Yo Ma and Emanuel Ax perform together is to witness a musical relationship shaped by more than four decades of friendship, trust, and curiosity. Ax has described their collaboration as one in which the music leads and the musicians follow. Their performances carry an ease and intimacy that only comes from years of listening closely to one another, responding in the moment, and returning again and again to the joy of making music together.

 

What makes this collaboration remarkable is not simply technical mastery. It is the sense of connection that runs through every note. Audiences can hear it in the way one musician follows the other’s lead, anticipates a phrase, or finds space for an unexpected idea to emerge.

 

Both artists are familiar faces at Carolina Performing Arts; Ma through multiple appearances with the Silkroad Ensemble and Ax through recitals and orchestral performances. Experiencing them together offers a rare opportunity to witness two lifelong friends in conversation through music.

 

Student tickets always $11. Eligible for CLE. Find out more and buy tickets at: https://carolinaperformingarts.org/events/emanuelax-yoyoma/

title: STREB EXTREME ACTION DO NOT TRY THIS AT HOME
location: Memorial Hall
description:
What can the human body do? Or maybe, what can it not do?

 

In DO NOT TRY THIS AT HOME, STREB performers—called “Action Heroes”—dive, fling, flip, and fall off of massive moving structures with split-second timing and fearless precision. Audiences gasp, laugh, tense up, and wonder how what they’re seeing is even possible.

 

Founder Elizabeth Streb has been called the Evel Knievel of dance, a thrill-seeker, and a Superwoman. She is the founder of SLAM—the STREB Lab for Action Mechanics—in Brooklyn, where her company has spent decades developing a movement practice called PopAction: a fusion acrobatics, rodeo, dance and athletics, rooted in a lifelong obsession with what happens to the human body when it is fully, fearlessly committed to motion. Her philosophy: “Anything too safe is not action.”

 

The company transforms physical risk into spectacles of wonder, exploring the outer extremes of human movement, asking what becomes possible when courage, creativity, athleticism, and engineering collide.

title: “To BEethoven Rather Than To Seem”: Part V | Gut Instinct Chamber Music Project
location: Person Hall
description:
FEATURING

Nicholas DiEguenio, violin
Mimi Solomon, piano

 

PROGRAM

Featuring Beethoven’s “Spring” Sonata and Robert Honstein’s Olmsted

This season, Gut Instinct takes on the large-scale project “To Beethoven Rather Than To Seem,” marking 200 years since Beethoven’s death and 250 since the U.S. Declaration of Independence. Over the course of five concerts, Nicholas DiEugenio and pianist Mimi Solomon will present all ten Beethoven Sonatas on period instruments along with five commissioned works written expressly for them.

 

PARKING

Please plan to arrive early as parking on campus can be tricky. Learn more about parking and directions to UNC-Chapel Hill’s campus.

 

The Gut Instinct Chamber Music Project, now in its third season, is a concert series in the Triangle area which brings UNC-Chapel Hill and Duke University’s historical instrument collections together with artists committed to presenting inspired, visceral, historically informed performances of the 19th-century chamber music repertoire. The series features music of female composers and their artistic circles. The name “Gut Instinct” is a play on words. In 19th-century Europe, the violin, viola, and cello were strung with (sheep) gut.

 

All of the artists collaborating with the Pleyel and Graf pianos at UNC-Chapel Hill (built in 19th-century Paris and Vienna, respectively), as well as the Clementi piano at Duke (early 19th-century England) use these gut string materials. The turn of phrase “gut instinct” also refers to the visceral, accessible nature of the musical performances that this series presents. Our mission is to make “Historically Informed Performance” accessible, relatable, and culturally relevant! We also want to feature these special pianos that are rarely heard by the public, along with great music by female composers which has remained lesser known to the greater public for far too long, and living composers who are keeping our art form alive!

title: Building an AI powered, global scale messaging system with XMPP &Deep Learning
description:
Triangle AI Meetup
This talk is an in-depth look at XMPP, the open standard for real-time messaging, and how to build a global scale, AI enhanced messaging system using XMPP. We’ll explore EJabberD, the massively scalable, open-source XMPP server that powers in-game chat for Eve Online, and examine how to: combine XMPP with WebRTC for real-time audio/video calling, add AIML to build helpful chatbots, and how to incorporate Deep Learning to categorize messages in real-time. After the talk, you’ll know how to use XMPP and Ejabberd to build anything from a help-desk chatops application, to a globe spanning in-game messaging system.
